Measured temperature rises appropriately and stabilizes without unresolved alarm. No red Inop. indicator or mattress sensor fault message is present. Alarm indicators and audible alarm respond during the facility-approved operational check. If the heater does not warm, overheats, displays sensor fault, or cannot maintain temperature, stop troubleshooting and escalate for repair. Expected outcome: The heated mattress function operates normally without persistent alarms before the device is released for patient use.

CCR.Complaint: NICU reported that the Babytherm 8010 displayed “Mattress temp. deviation above 1 °C” and the gel mattress did not appear to warm appropriately.
CCR.Cause: Verified correct gel mattress placement and normal power, but measured mattress temperature failed to approach the selected setpoint and the alarm recurred during evaluation without a patient.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the Babytherm 8010 from service, applied an Out of Service label, and routed the unit for bench evaluation of the heated mattress system.

helpfulDetails: Device confirmed as Babytherm 8010 or mattress-heater-equipped configuration
Mattress placed directly on heated tray surface
Gel mattress inspected for cracks, brittleness, leakage, folds, or kinks
Outlet tested and power status confirmed
Set mattress temperature and measured temperature
Presence of additional heat sources, including radiant warmer, phototherapy, or sunlight
Final device status: returned to service or removed from service

title: Drager Babytherm 8004 / 8010 Series Infant Warmer - DISPLAY OR CONTROL-PANEL FAILURE
description: Troubleshooting blank, dim, incomplete, flickering, or unresponsive control-panel displays before determining that internal repair is required.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions:
If the infant warmer is occupied or prepared for immediate patient use, notify clinical staff and transfer the patient to a known-working warming device before troubleshooting.

Do not rely on the Babytherm when the display is unreadable or controls cannot be confirmed, because temperature settings, measured values, alarms, and operating mode may not be safely verified.

Expected outcome: The patient is safely supported on alternate equipment before troubleshooting begins.

Why it matters: The Babytherm 8004/8010 uses its control panel and digital display to communicate warming settings, temperature information, text messages, and alarm conditions.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Reported
steps.instructions:
Power the unit only after it is removed from clinical use, then observe and document the condition:

Display completely blank
Display dim, flickering, or missing segments
Text display unreadable
Buttons do not respond
Alarm indicators do not illuminate
Settings cannot be adjusted or confirmed
On a Babytherm 8010, determine whether the failure involves the main radiant-heater controls, the heated-mattress controls, or both

Expected outcome: The symptom is clearly isolated before additional troubleshooting.

Why it matters: The Babytherm 8010 includes the heated gel mattress feature, while the 8004 does not include it as a standard feature; identifying which display area is affected helps narrow the failure.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Obvious External Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions:
Inspect the control-panel surface, display window, buttons, housing, power cord, plug, and surrounding warmer assembly for:

Cracks, impact damage, or fluid intrusion
Sticky or mechanically bound buttons
Evidence of cleaning-fluid residue
Damaged cord, loose plug, burn marks, unusual odor, or heat discoloration

Do not open the control housing or continue operating the unit if liquid intrusion, burning odor, overheating, or damaged power components are observed.

Expected outcome: No visible external condition explains the control-panel failure.

If damage or contamination is found: Remove the unit from service and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Verify AC Power to the Warmer
steps.instructions:
Confirm the warmer is connected directly to a known-working approved outlet. Inspect that the plug is fully seated and the power cord is intact. Test the outlet using facility-approved methods or a known-working device, as appropriate.

If the unit is plugged into an accessory power strip, isolation source, or movable power assembly, bypass questionable external sources only when permitted by facility policy.

Expected outcome: The warmer receives confirmed AC power.

If power is restored and the display functions normally: Complete required operational checks, document the corrected external power issue, and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Power-On Behavior and Alarm Indicators
steps.instructions:
Turn the warmer on and observe whether any display segments, indicator lights, alarm light, audible alarm, or startup activity occurs.

Document whether the failure is:

Total loss of power and display
Display failure with audible or visual alarm activity present
Partially operating panel with unresponsive keys
Intermittent display or control behavior when left stationary

Expected outcome: Power-on behavior indicates whether the problem affects the entire unit or primarily the operator interface.

Why it matters: The Babytherm includes a central alarm indicator and text-message display; alarm activity without readable control information still makes the device unsuitable for clinical use.

steps.title: 6. Confirm the Display Is Not Only Difficult to Read
steps.instructions:
If the display is illuminated but faint or difficult to read, view it from normal operator positions and assess whether ambient lighting, glare, or an abnormal contrast setting could explain the complaint.

Where accessible through normal operator controls and allowed by department procedure, verify whether display contrast adjustment restores readability. Do not enter advanced service procedures or change unrelated configuration settings.

Expected outcome: The display becomes clearly readable, or the symptom is confirmed as an equipment failure rather than a viewing or contrast issue.

If readability is restored: Verify normal operation and alarm visibility before returning the unit to service.

steps.title: 7. Perform the Available Operator-Panel Display and Indicator Check
steps.instructions:
Using the normal front-panel control intended to check LEDs, displays, annunciator, and audible alarm, observe whether the display segments, indicator lights, and audible alarm respond appropriately.

Document any portion of the test that does not respond, such as missing display segments, failed alarm indicator, absent tone, or nonresponsive key.

Expected outcome: All tested panel indications and alarm outputs respond correctly.

If any display, key, annunciator, or alarm indication fails: Do not return the warmer to patient use. The operating instructions identify a front-panel function for checking LEDs, displays, annunciator, and audible alarm.

steps.title: 8. Verify Basic Control Response Without Applying Patient Care
steps.instructions:
With the device out of service and unoccupied, confirm that normal operator controls respond consistently and that selections appear correctly on the display.

For the Babytherm 8010, separately verify whether the heated-mattress display/control area responds, because it is a model-specific control function.

Do not operate the heater for patient warming, bypass alarms, or leave a questionable unit available for use.

Expected outcome: Controls respond normally and displayed information remains stable.

If controls remain unresponsive, intermittent, or unreadable: Stop troubleshooting and escalate for repair evaluation.

steps.title: 9. Check for Repeatable Behavior After a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions:
If no damage, fluid intrusion, heat, or burning odor is present, perform one controlled power cycle with the unit out of service.

Observe whether the display/control-panel problem:

Clears and remains normal
Immediately recurs
Appears intermittently
Produces additional alarm or inoperative indications

Expected outcome: A repeatable result is obtained for documentation and repair triage.

If the problem clears after restart: The device should still complete appropriate functional and safety checks before return to service, and the intermittent complaint must be documented.

If the failure returns or remains present: Remove the unit from service and send it for bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Drager Babytherm 8010 powered on but the main control-panel display was unreadable and warming settings could not be confirmed.
CCR.Cause: Verified AC power and intact external cord; display remained blank during startup and did not respond correctly during the front-panel indicator/display check.
CCR.Resolution: Removed Babytherm 8010 from service, applied an Out of Service label, and routed the unit for bench evaluation of the display/control-panel system.

helpfulDetails: Whether the display was blank, dim, flickering, incomplete, or intermittent
Whether central alarm light or audible alarm activated
Whether the display/indicator check passed or failed
Whether the symptom affected the Babytherm 8010 heated-mattress controls
Evidence of fluid intrusion, unusual heat, or burning smell

title: Drager Babyleo TN500 IncuWarmer Infant Incubator - Heater Output / Temperature Regulation Fault
description: Troubleshooting heater output or temperature regulation faults caused by setup, airflow, sensor, accessory, or environmental issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the Babyleo TN500 is in use with a patient and there is a heater output or temperature regulation fault, do not continue troubleshooting while relying on the affected unit for thermal support. Move the infant to another approved warming or incubator device according to clinical procedure. Expected outcome: Patient temperature support is maintained on a known-good device. If this resolves the immediate care concern, stop and document the action taken.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported Fault
steps.instructions: Review the display and confirm the exact message, alarm, or temperature regulation behavior reported by staff. Note whether the issue involves: Low temperature alarm; High temperature alarm; Heater output not increasing; Temperature overshoot; Inconsistent air temperature; Skin temperature not matching expected trend; Fault appears during prewarming, incubator mode, radiant warmer mode, or transition between modes. Expected outcome: The fault type and operating mode are clearly identified.

steps.title: Check the Current Operating Mode and Temperature Setpoint
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the unit is operating in incubator mode, radiant warmer mode, manual mode, air temperature control, or skin temperature control. Verify that the selected setpoint matches the clinical expectation and is not unusually low or high. Expected outcome: The temperature regulation issue is not caused by an incorrect mode or setpoint selection. If correcting the mode or setpoint resolves the issue, return the device to clinical staff if appropriate and stop.

steps.title: Inspect for Open Panels, Access Doors, or Canopy Position Issues
steps.instructions: Check that the canopy, access doors, side panels, hand ports, and mattress area are properly closed and seated. An open panel or incomplete canopy closure can cause heat loss and unstable temperature regulation. Expected outcome: The patient compartment is properly enclosed for the selected mode. If closing or reseating a panel restores normal temperature control, document the finding and stop.

steps.title: Check for Airflow Obstruction
steps.instructions: Inspect the mattress area, air vents, warm air paths, and surrounding surfaces for blankets, positioning aids, tubing, labels, or supplies blocking airflow. Do not remove clinically required positioning items without clinical approval. Expected outcome: Air circulation paths are clear and the device can regulate temperature normally. If removing an obstruction resolves the issue, document what was found and stop.

steps.title: Verify Environmental Conditions Around the Unit
steps.instructions: Check whether the Babyleo is positioned near a draft, HVAC vent, open door, exterior wall, direct sunlight, portable fan, or other heat-producing equipment. Environmental changes can make the device appear to underheat, overheat, or regulate inconsistently. Expected outcome: The incubator is not being affected by external airflow or heat sources. If relocating the unit or correcting the environmental issue resolves the problem, stop and document.

steps.title: Inspect the Skin Temperature Probe and Placement
steps.instructions: If skin temperature control is being used, inspect the skin temperature probe for damage, contamination, loose connection, or improper placement. Confirm that the probe is secured properly and has good contact with the intended monitoring site. Expected outcome: The temperature probe is connected, intact, and positioned correctly. If a loose or misplaced probe caused the fault, correct the setup, verify stable temperature response, and stop.

steps.title: Swap the Skin Temperature Probe if Available
steps.instructions: If the fault appears related to skin temperature feedback, test with a known-good compatible skin temperature probe. Expected outcome: The unit responds normally with a known-good probe. If replacing the probe resolves the issue, remove the defective probe from service and document the accessory failure.

steps.title: Check for Contamination or Moisture Near Sensors and Air Paths
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible areas for spilled fluid, cleaning residue, condensation, lint, adhesive residue, or visible contamination. Do not open internal covers or perform deep disassembly during frontline troubleshooting. Expected outcome: No external contamination is affecting temperature sensing or airflow. If contamination is found externally, clean according to facility-approved procedures and reassess.

steps.title: Allow the Device to Stabilize After Setup Changes
steps.instructions: If the canopy, mode, setpoint, humidity, mattress position, or probe placement was recently changed, allow the device a reasonable stabilization period while monitoring displayed temperatures and alarms. Expected outcome: Temperature readings trend toward the selected setpoint without repeated faults. If the device stabilizes and alarms clear, document the adjustment and stop.

steps.title: Check Power Source and Startup Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the power cord is fully seated, the outlet is functioning, and the device is not operating with unstable power. Observe whether the heater fault appears immediately at startup or only after heating begins. Expected outcome: The unit has stable power and completes startup without recurring heater-related faults. If power correction resolves the issue, document the outlet or cord condition and stop.

steps.title: Compare Displayed Temperature Trends
steps.instructions: Compare the displayed air temperature, skin temperature, and set temperature trends if available. Look for obvious mismatch, sudden jumps, no change during heating, or readings that do not match the clinical environment. Expected outcome: Temperature feedback appears logical and changes gradually. If readings are erratic or physically unrealistic, suspect probe, sensor, or internal regulation fault and continue to escalation.

steps.title: Restart Only When Safe and Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the device is not supporting a patient, power the unit off, wait briefly, and restart it. Observe whether the same heater output or temperature regulation fault returns. Expected outcome: The unit restarts normally and does not repeat the heater fault. If the fault clears and does not return during observation, document the restart and monitor per facility policy.

steps.title: Remove From Service if the Fault Repeats
steps.instructions: If the heater output fault, temperature regulation fault, unstable temperature behavior, or sensor-related temperature issue returns after external checks, do not continue attempting repeated resets. Expected outcome: The unit is treated as unreliable for infant thermal support until evaluated.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the Drager Babyleo TN500 was alarming for temperature regulation and not maintaining the selected air temperature.
CCR.Cause: Found the canopy access panel not fully closed, causing heat loss and unstable temperature control.
CCR.Resolution: Closed and verified all access panels, observed temperature recovery toward setpoint, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact alarm or fault message displayed
Operating mode at time of fault
Set temperature and displayed air temperature
Accessories swapped, including whether the skin probe was swapped with a known-good probe
Canopy, hand ports, and panels checked
Airflow obstruction found or ruled out
Environmental factors, including drafts, vents, sunlight, or room conditions noted
Power behavior, including whether the outlet was tested and power cord condition was checked
Whether fault occurred at startup or during heating
Indicator lights, display messages, or heater status shown during the fault
Any unusual smell, heat, fan noise, or silence

title: Drager Babyleo TN500 IncuWarmer Infant Incubator - Humidity System Alarm or Low Humidity Performance
description: Troubleshooting humidity alarms, low humidity output, water supply issues, condensation, or humidity system performance concerns on the Babyleo TN500.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the Babyleo TN500 is actively supporting an infant and humidity performance is inadequate, notify clinical staff before troubleshooting. Confirm the infant remains thermally stable and that clinical staff determines whether another incubator or warming method is needed. Expected outcome: The infant is not left dependent on a device with unresolved humidity control concerns.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Alarm or Symptom
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact message or behavior reported. Check whether the issue is: Humidity system alarm; Humidity not reaching set value; Humidity dropping during use; Excessive condensation; Water reservoir or water supply warning; Humidity disabled or unavailable. Expected outcome: The reported condition is confirmed before parts or internal faults are suspected.

steps.title: Check Whether Humidity Is Actually Enabled
steps.instructions: Review the current operating mode and humidity setting. Confirm humidity is turned on and set appropriately for the clinical use case. Expected outcome: Humidity is enabled and has a valid setpoint. If humidity was disabled or set too low, correct the setting with clinical approval and monitor performance. If resolved, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Confirm the Device Is in Incubator Mode
steps.instructions: Humidity control is generally relevant when the device is being used as an incubator. Verify the canopy is closed and the device is not being used in a configuration where humidity control is limited or unavailable. Expected outcome: The Babyleo is in a mode that supports humidity operation.

steps.title: Inspect the Water Reservoir or Water Supply
steps.instructions: Check that the water reservoir is filled according to facility practice and manufacturer-approved water requirements. Confirm the reservoir is fully seated and not loose, empty, cracked, or incorrectly installed. Expected outcome: The humidity system has an available and properly installed water source. If the reservoir was empty or not seated correctly, correct the issue and allow time for humidity recovery. If resolved, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check for Incorrect or Non-Approved Water Use
steps.instructions: Verify that staff are using the correct water type per facility policy and manufacturer guidance. Look for evidence of mineral buildup, residue, discoloration, or contamination around the water reservoir area. Expected outcome: Water quality does not appear to be contributing to reduced humidity performance. If contamination or residue is present, remove the device from use for cleaning and evaluation per facility procedure.

steps.title: Inspect the Humidity Chamber and Accessible Water Path Areas
steps.instructions: Without disassembling internal components, inspect accessible areas for: Improperly seated parts; Visible debris; Water leakage; Cracks; Blocked openings; Heavy condensation outside expected areas. Expected outcome: No visible external obstruction or damage is affecting humidity delivery.

steps.title: Check the Canopy, Access Panels, and Door Seals
steps.instructions: Inspect the canopy, hand ports, access doors, tubing pass-throughs, and seals. Make sure all access panels close fully and that seals are not torn, folded, loose, or contaminated. Expected outcome: The incubator compartment can maintain a controlled humidity environment. Why it matters: Open ports or poor seals can cause humidity loss even if the humidity system is functioning.

steps.title: Verify Mattress Tray and Internal Components Are Properly Positioned
steps.instructions: Confirm the mattress tray, mattress, inner walls, and removable internal components are installed correctly. Look for gaps, misalignment, or anything preventing normal airflow inside the incubator compartment. Expected outcome: Airflow and humidity distribution are not being disrupted by incorrectly positioned components.

steps.title: Check for External Environmental Causes
steps.instructions: Review the surrounding environment for conditions that may reduce humidity performance, such as: Frequent canopy opening; High room airflow; Nearby vents; Cold ambient room temperature; Repeated access through hand ports; Device positioned near doors or drafts. Expected outcome: External conditions are not causing excessive humidity loss. If environmental factors are present, correct them and reassess humidity performance.

steps.title: Allow Adequate Time for Humidity to Stabilize
steps.instructions: After filling water, closing the canopy, or changing the humidity setpoint, allow the system time to stabilize. Do not assume failure immediately after setup unless an alarm persists or the humidity does not trend upward. Expected outcome: Humidity begins moving toward the set value over time.

steps.title: Inspect for Leaks or Unusual Water Behavior
steps.instructions: Look around the water reservoir area, base, mattress area, and visible humidification path for leakage. Check whether water is collecting where it should not be. Expected outcome: No abnormal leakage, pooling, or dripping is present. If leakage is found, remove the device from service and send it for evaluation.

steps.title: Check for Excessive Condensation
steps.instructions: If the complaint is low humidity but condensation is present, determine whether the issue may be sensor reading, airflow, temperature difference, or compartment condition rather than lack of water vapor. Confirm doors and canopy are closed and that incubator temperature is stable. Expected outcome: The humidity complaint is not misinterpreted due to condensation or unstable temperature conditions.

steps.title: Power Cycle Only When Safe
steps.instructions: If the device is not supporting an active patient, power the Babyleo TN500 off and back on. Observe whether the humidity alarm returns during startup or after humidity is enabled. Expected outcome: A temporary software or startup condition clears and humidity operation returns. If the alarm clears and humidity performance returns to normal, document the result and return the device according to facility policy.

steps.title: Check Alarm History or Event Information If Available
steps.instructions: Review any accessible alarm history, event log, or displayed fault information without entering service-level procedures beyond your facility authorization. Note exact alarm wording, timing, and whether the issue repeats. Expected outcome: The fault pattern is documented for repair evaluation if needed.

steps.title: Test With the Device Empty and Off Patient
steps.instructions: If clinically available, remove the device from patient use and perform a controlled operational check. Set the device up with water installed, canopy closed, humidity enabled, and allow it to run under observation. Expected outcome: Humidity should trend upward without repeated alarms, leaks, abnormal sounds, or unusual odor. If the alarm repeats or humidity does not improve, stop troubleshooting and escalate.

CCR.Complaint: NICU staff reported a humidity system alarm on a Drager Babyleo TN500 and stated humidity was not reaching the ordered setpoint.
CCR.Cause: Water reservoir was found nearly empty and the canopy access port was not fully latched, causing poor humidity recovery.
CCR.Resolution: Filled and reseated the water reservoir, secured the access port, verified humidity enabled, monitored upward humidity trend, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Humidity setpoint and actual displayed humidity
Whether the canopy was open or closed
Water reservoir level and seating condition
Door, hand port, and seal condition
Evidence of leaks, pooling, or condensation
Ambient room conditions or nearby airflow
Whether the alarm repeated after power cycle
Indicator lights or displayed warnings related to humidity, water supply, or system status
Accessories or removable components checked or repositioned
Power behavior during startup, power cycle, or alarm recovery

title: Drager Babyleo TN500 IncuWarmer Infant Incubator - Skin Probe, Air Temp Sensor, or Sensor Module Reading Error
description: Troubleshooting temperature sensor reading errors, unstable readings, probe connection issues, or sensor module faults on the Babyleo TN500.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the Babyleo TN500 is in active patient use and a temperature reading error is present, notify clinical staff immediately. Do not continue relying on an inaccurate skin or air temperature reading for patient thermal regulation. If patient temperature control is affected, clinical staff should move the infant to another verified warming device or use an approved backup method. Expected outcome: The infant is not dependent on a device with unreliable temperature feedback.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported Sensor Error
steps.instructions: Look at the display and confirm whether the problem involves: Skin temperature probe; Air temperature sensor; Sensor module; Intermittent temperature reading; Missing or unrealistic temperature value; Alarm or message related to temperature measurement. Note whether the issue occurs at startup, during warm-up, during incubator mode, during radiant warmer mode, or only after the device is moved. Expected outcome: The exact sensor-related symptom is identified before troubleshooting continues.

steps.title: Check for Obvious Environmental or Patient Setup Issues
steps.instructions: Verify that doors, portholes, access panels, canopy position, and mattress area are properly configured for the selected operating mode. Large air leaks, open panels, or incorrect canopy position can affect air temperature stability and may make the issue appear sensor-related. Expected outcome: The incubator environment is physically set up correctly. If closing panels or correcting the setup restores normal readings, document the finding and stop.

steps.title: Inspect the Skin Temperature Probe Placement
steps.instructions: If the issue involves skin temperature, confirm that the probe is properly attached to the infant per clinical procedure. Look for a loose probe, detached reflective cover, probe placed over clothing, probe placed in an unsuitable location, or probe pulled away from the skin. Clinical staff should verify placement; Clinical Engineering should not reposition the probe on the patient without appropriate clinical involvement. Expected outcome: The probe is making proper patient contact and is being used correctly. If correct placement restores a stable reading, return the device to use after confirming normal operation.

steps.title: Inspect the Skin Probe Cable and Connector
steps.instructions: Remove the device from active patient use before handling patient-connected accessories. Check the skin probe and cable for: Cuts; Pinched cable insulation; Bent or damaged connector pins; Fluid contamination; Tape residue near the probe; Loose connection at the sensor input. Reseat the probe connector firmly. Expected outcome: The probe cable and connector are clean, intact, and fully seated. If the reading returns and remains stable after reseating, document the loose connection and stop.

steps.title: Swap the Skin Probe with a Known-Good Probe
steps.instructions: If available, install a known-good compatible Drager skin temperature probe. Observe whether the reading returns, stabilizes, or the alarm clears. Expected outcome: A failed or damaged probe is separated from a device-side issue. If the known-good probe works normally, replace the defective probe, document the accessory failure, and return the unit to service if all checks pass.

steps.title: Check for Probe Port Contamination or Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect the probe input area for visible contamination, fluid residue, corrosion, cracked plastic, or looseness. Do not insert tools into the connector or attempt internal repair. Expected outcome: The probe port appears clean, secure, and physically undamaged. If the port is damaged or contaminated beyond basic external cleaning, remove the unit from service for bench evaluation.

steps.title: Verify Air Temperature Sensor Path Is Not Blocked
steps.instructions: If the issue involves air temperature readings, inspect the air sensor area and airflow path for obstruction. Check for linens, positioning aids, equipment, covers, tape, or supplies blocking airflow near the sensor area. Expected outcome: Air can circulate normally and the sensor is not being externally blocked. If removing the obstruction restores normal temperature behavior, document the obstruction and stop.

steps.title: Check for Recent Cleaning or Fluid Exposure
steps.instructions: Ask staff whether the unit was recently cleaned, moved, or exposed to fluid. Moisture near temperature sensors, cable ports, or the sensor module area can cause unstable readings or sensor alarms. Look for visible liquid, cleaning residue, or unusual smell. Expected outcome: No evidence of fluid intrusion or residue affecting sensor operation. If fluid exposure is suspected, remove the device from service and send it for inspection.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device Only When Safe
steps.instructions: If the device is not supporting an active patient, perform a normal power cycle. Allow the Babyleo TN500 to restart and complete its startup checks. Recheck whether the sensor reading, alarm, or module message returns. Expected outcome: A temporary software or communication condition clears after restart. If the error clears and all temperature readings remain stable during observation, document the action and return the unit to service according to facility policy.

steps.title: Check Whether the Error Follows a Specific Accessory or Stays with the Unit
steps.instructions: Test with known-good external accessories where available. Determine whether the problem follows: One skin probe; One connector; One sensor module condition; The Babyleo unit itself. Expected outcome: Troubleshooting identifies whether the issue is accessory-related or device-related. If the problem stays with the unit after accessory replacement, suspect internal sensor module, connector, or control system fault.

steps.title: Observe Temperature Reading Stability
steps.instructions: With no patient connected and only when safe, observe the displayed temperature values for stability. Watch for readings that are missing, jump rapidly, remain unrealistic, or trigger repeated alarms. Expected outcome: Temperature readings are reasonable and stable during observation. If readings remain erratic after external checks, remove the unit from service.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that the Drager Babyleo TN500 displayed a skin temperature probe error and would not maintain a stable skin temperature reading.
CCR.Cause: Found damaged insulation near the skin probe connector; known-good compatible probe produced a stable temperature reading with no recurring alarm.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the defective skin temperature probe, verified stable temperature display during observation, and returned the Babyleo TN500 to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact sensor message or alarm displayed
Whether the issue involved skin temperature, air temperature, or sensor module
Whether the device was in incubator mode or radiant warmer mode
Doors, portholes, and canopy position verified
Any signs of fluid exposure or cleaning residue
Whether power cycle cleared the issue
Whether the reading was missing, unstable, or unrealistic

title: Drager Babyleo TN500 IncuWarmer Infant Incubator - Integrated Scale Will Not Zero Or Gives Inaccurate Weight
description: Troubleshooting integrated scale zeroing or inaccurate weight issues caused by setup, mattress load, accessories, patient contact, or scale obstruction.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the Babyleo TN500 is in active patient use, do not remove supports, reposition accessories, or manipulate the mattress area without clinical staff involvement. Have clinical staff determine whether the infant can be safely moved, held, or temporarily supported during scale troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient safety and thermal support are maintained before any scale checks begin.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported Scale Issue
steps.instructions: Verify whether the issue is: Scale will not zero; Weight reading is unstable; Weight is clearly inaccurate; Weight changes when nothing was added or removed; Scale alarms, prompts, or errors are present. Expected outcome: The exact scale complaint is confirmed before parts or device failure are assumed.

steps.title: Check That the Device Is Stable and Not Being Moved
steps.instructions: Confirm the Babyleo is on a level surface with wheels locked and no one leaning on the incubator, mattress tray, side panels, or accessory rails. Expected outcome: The weight reading should stabilize when the unit is stationary and not being physically disturbed. If this resolves the issue, stop and document the cause.

steps.title: Verify Nothing Is Touching or Binding the Weighing Surface
steps.instructions: Inspect around the mattress platform for anything contacting the bed frame, side panels, incubator wall, tubing, blankets, positioning aids, or cables. Look for items that may be resting partly on the mattress and partly on the incubator frame, because this can unload or add force to the scale. Expected outcome: The mattress area should be free-floating without external contact affecting the scale reading. If this resolves the issue, stop and document the obstruction or contact point.

steps.title: Remove Nonessential Items Before Zeroing
steps.instructions: With clinical approval, remove extra blankets, gel pads, positioning rolls, supplies, toys, paperwork, or loose equipment from the mattress area. Only items intended to be included in the tare/zero process should remain. Expected outcome: The scale should zero more reliably when unnecessary added weight is removed.

steps.title: Check Mattress and Pad Position
steps.instructions: Confirm the mattress, mattress cover, and any approved pad are seated correctly and not folded, wedged, or caught under an edge. A shifted or pinched mattress can interfere with weight transfer to the scale system. Expected outcome: The mattress should sit flat and centered without rubbing or binding. If correcting the mattress position restores normal scale function, stop and document.

steps.title: Verify Tubing, Cables, and Sensors Are Not Pulling on the Patient or Mattress
steps.instructions: Check IV lines, respiratory tubing, temperature probes, SpO₂ cables, ECG leads, and other patient connections. Make sure they have enough slack and are not pulling upward, downward, or sideways on the infant or mattress. Expected outcome: The scale reading should not be affected by external tension from patient connections.

steps.title: Reattempt the Zero/Tare Process Under Proper Conditions
steps.instructions: Follow the facility-approved operating procedure for zeroing the integrated scale. Confirm the correct items are present during zeroing and that the mattress area is not touched during the process. Expected outcome: The scale should complete zeroing and provide a stable baseline. If zeroing completes successfully, stop and document the setup correction.

steps.title: Compare With a Known-Good Reference Method
steps.instructions: If the weight still appears inaccurate, ask clinical staff to compare the reading with an approved backup scale or recent verified patient weight, if clinically appropriate. Do not use the integrated scale for patient weight decisions if the reading is questionable. Expected outcome: The suspected scale error is confirmed or ruled out against a reliable reference.

steps.title: Check for Repeated Error After Restart
steps.instructions: If safe and allowed by facility procedure, power cycle or restart the device when it is not actively supporting a patient’s immediate care needs. After restart, repeat the scale check with the mattress area properly prepared. Expected outcome: A temporary software or initialization issue may clear after restart. If the scale still will not zero or remains inaccurate, remove the scale function from clinical use and escalate.

steps.title: Inspect for Obvious Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: Look externally for signs of fluid intrusion, cracked mattress support components, damaged scale area, loose panels, missing parts, or anything abnormal around the bed platform. Do not disassemble the weighing mechanism or access internal load cell components during basic troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Any visible damage or contamination is identified for repair evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: NICU staff reported the Babyleo TN500 integrated scale would not zero and displayed inconsistent infant weight readings.
CCR.Cause: Found mattress pad partially shifted and patient tubing pulling against the mattress surface during the zeroing process.
CCR.Resolution: Repositioned mattress pad, relieved tubing tension, repeated zero process successfully, and verified stable scale reading with staff present.

helpfulDetails: Whether the unit was occupied or empty during troubleshooting
Whether the scale would not zero or gave unstable readings
Extra blankets, gel pads, or accessories present
Whether a backup scale was used for comparison
Power behavior or whether restart changed the behavior
Environmental factors such as unit movement, uneven floor, leaning on the device, or accessories contacting the scale surface
Any displayed scale message, alarm, indicator light, prompt, or error
Any visible damage, fluid exposure, or contamination

title: Drager Babyleo TN500 IncuWarmer Infant Incubator - Canopy Lift, Side Access Panel, or Bed Tilt Positioning Issue
description: Troubleshooting canopy lift, access panel, or bed tilt issues caused by obstruction, lockout, misalignment, accessory interference, or mechanical wear.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the Babyleo TN500 is occupied, do not attempt repeated canopy, panel, or bed movement while the infant is receiving care. Confirm with clinical staff before moving the canopy, opening panels, adjusting bed tilt, or changing access configuration. Expected outcome: The patient is protected from sudden movement, temperature disruption, or accidental contact. Why it matters: The Babyleo TN500 supports neonatal thermoregulation, and unnecessary opening or movement can affect the care environment.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Positioning Issue
steps.instructions: Identify the exact problem reported: Canopy will not raise; Canopy will not lower; Canopy movement feels stiff or uneven; Side access panel will not latch; Side access panel drops open or feels loose; Hand port or panel does not close securely; Bed tilt will not adjust; Bed tilt moves unevenly or does not hold position. Expected outcome: The complaint is narrowed to canopy, access panel, or bed tilt operation. Why it matters: These are different mechanical systems and should not be treated as one generic incubator failure.

steps.title: Check for Patient Care Accessories or Obstructions
steps.instructions: Inspect around the canopy, bed, panels, and mattress tray for anything blocking movement. Check for: Tubing caught near the canopy or hinge area; ECG, temperature probe, SpO₂, or oxygen tubing routed through a moving area; Blankets, positioning aids, nests, or gel pads interfering with bed tilt; IV lines or ventilator tubing pulling against the side panel; Items stored near the base or lift path. Remove or reroute only when clinically safe and with staff awareness. Expected outcome: The canopy, side panel, or bed tilt moves normally after the obstruction is cleared. If this resolves the issue, return the device to service if no damage is found and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Confirm the Device Is Not in a Locked or Restricted State
steps.instructions: Check the user interface for any lockout, screen lock, or restricted adjustment condition affecting height, bed tilt, or device movement. Drager product information notes that the Babyleo TN500 includes lock functions for screen, height adjustment, and bed tilt to help prevent accidental adjustment. Expected outcome: Movement controls respond after the lock condition is cleared by authorized staff. If this resolves the issue, document the lockout condition and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Inspect the Side Access Panels and Hand Ports
steps.instructions: Open and close the affected panel slowly. Check for: Panel not seated evenly; Latch not engaging; Loose, cracked, or damaged latch parts; Debris, tape, labels, or dried residue around the latch; Hand port door not fully closed; Gasket or seal displaced from its normal position. Do not force the panel closed. Expected outcome: The panel closes smoothly and locks securely. Why it matters: Drager instructions emphasize checking that side access panels, the front access panel, and hand ports lock securely and repairing them if necessary.

steps.title: Check for Cleaning Residue or Fluid Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect hinge points, latch areas, panel edges, and bed tilt contact areas for sticky residue, cleaning chemical buildup, or spilled fluid. Clean external surfaces according to facility-approved procedures and allow the area to dry. Expected outcome: Movement improves after external residue is removed. If movement remains stiff, uneven, or unreliable after cleaning, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check Canopy Movement Without Forcing It
steps.instructions: When the patient is not in the device, carefully test canopy movement through its normal range. Observe for: Binding; Uneven movement; Grinding, clicking, or popping sounds; Canopy stopping before full travel; Canopy not staying in position; Excessive looseness or wobble. Expected outcome: The canopy opens and closes smoothly without abnormal noise or resistance. Do not force the canopy if resistance is present.

steps.title: Inspect the Canopy Area for Misalignment or Damage
steps.instructions: Visually check the canopy, hinge area, and surrounding frame. Look for: Cracked canopy material; Bent hinge hardware; Uneven gap between canopy and frame; Loose covers; Signs of impact; Missing screws or hardware; Canopy rubbing against another surface. Expected outcome: No visible damage or misalignment is present. If damage is found, remove the device from service and escalate for repair.

steps.title: Verify Bed Tilt Operation
steps.instructions: With the patient removed or when clinically safe, operate the bed tilt adjustment through its normal range. Confirm whether: Tilt responds in both directions; Movement is smooth; Bed returns to a level position; Bed holds the selected position; One side appears lower or unstable; Controls respond normally. Drager describes the Babyleo TN500 as having an adjustable mattress tray height and tilt. Expected outcome: Bed tilt operates smoothly and maintains position.

steps.title: Check for Mattress Tray or Bed Support Interference
steps.instructions: Inspect the mattress tray, bed support, scale area if equipped, and accessory placement. Look for: Mattress not seated correctly; Positioning aids interfering with tray movement; Foreign object under or beside the bed platform; Bed support not fully seated; Accessory mounted in a way that contacts the bed during tilt. Expected outcome: Bed tilt returns to normal once the interference is removed. If this resolves the issue, document the obstruction and verify full movement before returning the unit to use.

steps.title: Check for Signs of Mechanical Wear or Unsafe Movement
steps.instructions: Remove the device from service if any of the following are found: Canopy drops, slips, or will not stay open; Side panel will not latch securely; Panel hinge is cracked or loose; Bed tilt does not hold position; Bed platform feels unstable; Abnormal grinding, popping, or binding occurs; Any patient access component appears damaged. Expected outcome: Unsafe mechanical conditions are not left in clinical use.

steps.title: Perform a Final Functional Check
steps.instructions: If no damage is found and the issue was corrected externally, verify: Canopy opens and closes smoothly; Side access panels latch securely; Hand ports close properly; Bed tilt adjusts and holds position; No tubing or accessories interfere with motion; No unusual noise, looseness, or instability is present. Expected outcome: Device movement is safe, repeatable, and ready for clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: NICU staff reported that the Babyleo TN500 side access panel would not latch securely after patient care.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the side panel latch area had dried residue and the panel was not seating fully.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned the external latch area, verified both side access panels and hand ports locked securely, confirmed canopy and bed tilt movement, and returned device to service.

helpfulDetails: Hand ports checked for secure closure
Bed tilt tested in both directions
Lockout or screen lock status checked
Any abnormal noise, binding, or looseness
Visible damage to canopy, latch, hinge, or bed platform

title: Drager Perseus Anesthesia Machine - Breathing System Leak or Leak Test Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed leakage tests or excessive breathing-system leakage caused by loose circuits, absorbers, sampling components, vaporizers, seals, or incorrect assembly.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform a system test, leakage test, or extended troubleshooting while a patient is connected to the anesthesia machine. If a leak is suspected during a procedure: Move ventilation to another verified anesthesia machine or approved backup method. Follow the facility’s anesthesia emergency procedures. Remove the affected Perseus from clinical reliance once patient care is stabilized. Expected: Patient ventilation and anesthetic delivery are maintained using verified equipment. The Perseus pressurizes the breathing system during testing, and the manufacturer specifically warns not to perform the system test with a patient connected.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Review the test screen and determine whether the reported problem is: Complete system-test failure; Breathing-system test failure; Leakage-test failure; Excessive displayed leakage; A leak that occurs only with a specific circuit or vaporizer installed; A failure that began after cleaning, accessory replacement, or absorber replacement. Record any displayed test details, affected subsystem, leakage value, and color-coded result. Expected: The complaint is narrowed to a repeatable test condition rather than a general report that the machine “leaks.”

steps.title: 3. Confirm the Device Is Prepared Exactly as Directed
steps.instructions: Place the Perseus in Standby and prepare it according to the on-screen checklist. Verify: No patient is connected. The circuit plug is installed where directed. Flexible hoses are extended to their intended working length. Required gas supplies are available. The breathing bag and breathing circuit are configured as shown on the screen. No test step has been skipped or accepted without correction. Repeat the applicable automatic test. Expected: The test completes successfully when the machine is configured correctly. If the test passes, document the configuration error and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Breathing Circuit and Patient Connections
steps.instructions: Check the inspiratory and expiratory hoses, Y-piece, filters, adapters, test plug, and breathing bag. Look for: Loose or partially seated connections; Cracked, stretched, punctured, or crushed hoses; Damaged Y-piece or circuit plug; Incorrectly installed filters or adapters; A leaking or improperly connected breathing bag; Incompatible or recently substituted accessories. Reseat each connection firmly. Replace questionable disposable components with verified compatible items, then repeat the leakage test. Expected: Leakage decreases and the test passes after a defective or poorly seated circuit component is corrected.

steps.title: 5. Check the CO2 Absorber Assembly
steps.instructions: Inspect the CO2 absorber or CLIC absorber assembly. Verify: The absorber is fully inserted and locked. The absorber container is properly closed. The CLIC adapter is securely attached. No sealing surface is visibly dirty, folded, damaged, or obstructed. The absorber was assembled correctly after filling or replacement. The manufacturer identifies an improperly secured absorber or CLIC adapter as a possible leakage source. Repeat the leakage test after reseating or replacing the absorber assembly. Expected: The test passes when the absorber and its sealing surfaces are correctly seated.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the APL Valve and Breathing-Bag Connection
steps.instructions: Verify that the APL valve is correctly installed, securely seated, and positioned as required by the on-screen test instructions. Inspect the breathing-bag connection, bag elbow, and optional flexible bag arm. Check for: Loose threaded or push-fit connections; Incorrectly seated flexible arm; Damaged bag-arm sealing ring; Cracked elbow or connector; APL valve that was incorrectly reinstalled after cleaning. Do not disassemble the valve internally. Correct only external fitment or replace a visibly damaged approved component. Expected: The leak test passes after the APL valve or bag assembly is correctly seated.

steps.title: 7. Check the Water Trap and Sample Line
steps.instructions: Inspect the gas-monitoring sampling path. Verify: The water trap is installed and fully seated. The sample line is connected at both ends. The sample line is not kinked, split, loose, or leaking. Sample-line fittings are undamaged. The water trap is not cracked, overfilled, or incorrectly installed. Replace the sample line or water trap with verified compatible components when damage is suspected. Expected: The leakage test passes after the sampling system is restored to a sealed condition.

steps.title: 8. Inspect External Breathing-System Seating
steps.instructions: If the failure began after cleaning or breathing-system replacement, verify that the removable breathing system is fully seated and locked into the machine. Check externally that: The breathing-system housing is sitting flush. Locking levers are fully engaged. Inspiratory and expiratory ports are secure. Flow-sensor ports are properly seated. No visible O-ring is missing, pinched, contaminated, or displaced. The breathing-system cover does not prevent complete seating. Do not proceed into internal pneumatic disassembly. Expected: The test passes after correcting an incomplete installation or externally visible seal problem.

steps.title: 9. Isolate Vaporizers as a Possible Leak Source
steps.instructions: Ensure each vaporizer is: Upright and fully seated on its mounting adapter; Locked into position; Set to the off or zero position; Properly closed at its filling and draining connections; Free from visible damage or leakage. Run the leakage test with the vaporizers configured as directed by the on-screen instructions. When appropriate and permitted by facility procedure, test one vaporizer at a time or remove a suspect vaporizer to determine whether the failure follows it. The Perseus leakage assistant can support evaluation of breathing-system, circuit, and vaporizer leakage by continuously displaying test pressure and leakage changes. Expected: The failure is isolated to a particular vaporizer or mounting position. If the test passes without one vaporizer, remove that vaporizer from service for separate evaluation.

steps.title: 10. Use the Leakage Assistant
steps.instructions: From the test details screen, open the Leakage Assistant and follow the displayed instructions. While the system maintains test pressure: Gently reseat one external connection at a time. Watch for a meaningful change in the displayed leakage value. Avoid changing several components simultaneously. Repeat the component test after correcting the suspected source. The manufacturer recommends systematic leak localization by isolating individual components and using the leakage assistant when needed. Expected: A specific circuit, absorber, sampling component, vaporizer, or breathing-system connection is identified. If the test passes, complete a full operational checkout before returning the machine to service.

CCR.Complaint: Anesthesia staff reported that the Drager Perseus failed its pre-use leakage test and displayed excessive breathing-system leakage.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the CO2 absorber incompletely seated, preventing the absorber seal from closing properly.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated and locked the absorber, repeated the leakage and system tests successfully, completed an operational checkout, and returned the machine to service.

helpfulDetails: Patient connected when issue occurred: Yes / No
Exact failed test and displayed leakage value
Test result color or restriction message
CO2 absorber and CLIC adapter checked
Water trap and sample line checked
APL valve and bag arm checked
Issue began after cleaning or accessory replacement
Unusual gas odor, sound, heat, or visible damage

title: Drager Perseus Anesthesia Machine - Flow Sensor Calibration Failure or Unstable Volume Measurement
description: Troubleshooting failed flow-sensor calibration or unstable tidal and minute-volume readings caused by test status, leaks, moisture, sensor seating, contamination, or sensor failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the Perseus is connected to an active patient. Coordinate with the anesthesia provider to: Transfer ventilation to another verified anesthesia machine or approved backup method. Maintain appropriate independent patient monitoring. Move the affected Perseus to Standby before testing. Expected: Patient care is no longer dependent on equipment with questionable volume measurement. Why it matters: Failed flow sensing may affect ventilation and monitoring. The system test must not be performed while a patient is connected because the breathing system is pressurized during testing. If safe backup ventilation and monitoring are established, continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Complaint
steps.instructions: Review the reported message and determine whether the problem involves: Flow sensor calibration required; Inspiratory flow sensor not calibrated; Expiratory flow sensor not calibrated; Unstable inspiratory tidal volume; Unstable expiratory tidal volume; Large or inconsistent differences between inspired and expired volume; Fluctuating minute-volume readings; Volume-controlled ventilation failure. Record whether the problem began after breathing-system removal, reprocessing, flow-sensor replacement, or circuit changes. Expected: The affected sensor and operating condition are identified. A disconnected or replaced breathing system, an uncalibrated sensor, and flow-sensor failure may cause inspiratory or expiratory flow-sensor calibration alarms.

steps.title: 3. Check Calibration and System-Test Status
steps.instructions: From Standby, review the most recent system-test results and determine whether flow-sensor calibration is overdue or incomplete. The Flow sensor calibration required message may occur when: The sensors have not been calibrated since power-up. More than 24 hours have passed since the last calibration. The breathing system or sensor was removed after calibration. Run the guided breathing-system test or full system test as appropriate. Expected: The test completes successfully and the calibration message clears. The breathing-system test calibrates the flow sensors, includes leakage testing, and should be completed after flow-sensor or breathing-system replacement. If calibration passes and measurements stabilize, document the result and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the External Breathing Circuit
steps.instructions: Check the complete test configuration for: Loose inspiratory or expiratory hose connections; Cracked, stretched, or incorrectly connected hoses; Loose Y-piece, test lung, filter, or breathing bag; Incorrectly seated absorber; Open sampling ports; Excessive condensate; Occluded or saturated filters; Incorrect circuit configuration for the selected patient category. Reconnect or replace questionable external accessories and repeat the leakage or breathing-system test. Expected: The circuit passes its leakage check and volume readings remain stable over repeated breaths. Why it matters: Circuit leakage can reduce the delivered or measured volume and create differences between inspired and expired readings. If correcting a circuit problem resolves the measurement instability, stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Flow-Sensor Installation
steps.instructions: With the machine in Standby and prepared according to facility procedures, inspect the accessible inspiratory and expiratory flow-sensor assemblies. Verify that: Each sensor is installed in the correct port. Both ports are fully inserted and tightened. The sensor body is not reversed, tilted, or partially seated. Required seals and O-rings are present. The surrounding breathing-system housing is seated correctly. Do not force the sensors or ports. Expected: Both sensors are correctly installed without looseness, missing seals, or visible misalignment. Improperly installed or damaged flow sensors and missing O-rings may cause breathing-system leakage. After reseating a sensor, repeat the breathing-system test. If the test passes, stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect for Moisture, Deposits, or Damage
steps.instructions: Visually inspect each accessible flow sensor for: Condensate; Disinfectant residue; Lint or fibers; Dried secretions; Aerosol deposits; Cracks, discoloration, or deformation; Damaged internal measuring elements. Do not insert tools, brushes, compressed air, or test probes into the sensor. Confirm that any recently reprocessed component is completely dry and was processed according to its specific instructions. Expected: Sensors are clean, dry, and visibly undamaged. Deposits or reprocessing contamination may damage the measuring elements. Replace the sensor when deposits remain or visible damage is present.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Flow Sensor
steps.instructions: When permitted by facility policy, replace the suspected inspiratory or expiratory sensor with a compatible, known-good sensor. Replace one sensor at a time when practical so the failed component can be identified. After each replacement: Confirm correct installation. Run the breathing-system test. Review the sensor-specific test result. Recheck displayed volume stability. Expected: Calibration succeeds and stable volume measurement returns after replacing the defective sensor. If replacement resolves the issue, stop and retain the failed sensor according to facility procedures.

steps.title: 8. Verify Volume Performance
steps.instructions: Connect a calibrated anesthesia-machine analyzer and approved test lung. Using a controlled test configuration: Deliver several consistent breaths. Observe inspired tidal volume, expired tidal volume, and minute volume. Watch for drifting or breath-to-breath instability. Check whether the problem occurs in multiple ventilation modes. Compare displayed and analyzer measurements using applicable manufacturer specifications and facility acceptance limits. Expected: Measurements remain repeatable and within approved limits without flow-sensor alarms. Do not return the machine to service based only on a cleared alarm. Confirm actual functional performance.

steps.title: 9. Review Test Results and Device Logs
steps.instructions: Record: Exact alarm text; Inspiratory or expiratory sensor involved; System-test and breathing-system-test results; Leakage result; Sensors or accessories exchanged; Analyzer readings; Whether the failure followed reprocessing or breathing-system removal. If the test identifies another correctable external issue, address it and repeat the complete test. Expected: The final device status and failure pattern are clearly established.

CCR.Complaint: Anesthesia staff reported repeated “Expiratory flow sensor not calibrated” alarms and unstable expired tidal-volume readings during pre-use testing.
CCR.Cause: Expiratory flow sensor had visible residue and continued to fail the breathing-system test after reseating; the circuit passed leakage testing.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the expiratory flow sensor, completed a successful breathing-system test, and verified stable tidal and minute-volume measurements with a calibrated analyzer.

helpfulDetails: Breathing system recently removed or reprocessed

title: Drager Perseus Anesthesia Machine - O2 Sensor Calibration Failure or Incorrect FiO2 Reading
description: Troubleshooting failed O2-sensor calibration or implausible FiO2 values caused by gas supply, sampling-path, water-trap, circuit, test, or internal measurement faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the anesthesia machine is connected to an active patient. If the displayed FiO2 is questionable during a procedure: Notify the anesthesia provider immediately. Use an independent oxygen-monitoring system. Transfer ventilation and anesthesia delivery to another verified machine when directed. Do not rely on a questionable FiO2 value for clinical decisions. Expected: Patient ventilation and oxygen monitoring are maintained using verified equipment. If patient care has been safely transferred, continue troubleshooting off patient.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Being Reported
steps.instructions: Review the alarm message, staff report, system-test result, and device logbook. Determine whether the complaint involves: O2 sensor failure; FiO2 low or FiO2 high; O2 fresh-gas flow measurement failure; No O2 delivery; O2 supply low; An O2-related system-test or calibration failure; A displayed FiO2 that does not match an independent analyzer. Expected: The issue is classified as a gas-supply, fresh-gas delivery, sampling-path, or patient-gas measurement problem. These alarms represent different conditions. An O2 sensor failure may involve the patient-gas measurement system, while O2 supply and fresh-gas flow alarms involve separate delivery systems.

steps.title: 3. Verify Power and Allow a Complete Startup
steps.instructions: Connect the machine to a known-good AC receptacle and confirm normal mains-power indication. Restart the device only when permitted by facility procedure. Allow it to complete its startup sequence without interruption. Check for: Power interruptions during startup; Abnormal boot messages; Additional sensor or gas-measurement alarms; A system test that was canceled or bypassed. Expected: The machine reaches Standby normally and is ready to perform its system test. If a normal restart clears the condition and subsequent testing passes, complete functional verification, document the result, and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check the Oxygen Supply
steps.instructions: Inspect the external O2 supply before assuming that the sensor has failed. Verify: The O2 pipeline hose is fully connected at the wall outlet and machine inlet. The pipeline outlet provides the expected supply pressure. The backup O2 cylinder is properly mounted and sufficiently filled. Cylinder valves and pressure indications agree with the machine status display. No O2 supply or delivery alarm is present. Expected: A stable medical O2 source is available to the machine without supply-related alarms. An absent or unstable O2 supply can cause unexpected oxygen values and failed system testing without indicating an internal O2 sensor defect. If correcting the supply restores normal readings and testing, document the cause and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Sample Line
steps.instructions: Follow the sample line from the patient connection to the water trap. Check for: Loose connections; Cracks or cuts; Kinks or compression; Moisture accumulation; Internal blockage; Incorrect routing; Nonapproved adapters or sample tubing; Connection to an inappropriate circuit port. Confirm the line is securely attached at the approved sampling location and at the water trap. Expected: The sample line is open, dry, correctly routed, and securely connected. A damaged, blocked, or improperly connected sample line can produce faulty gas measurements. Replace a questionable disposable sample line. If readings normalize, complete testing and stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Water Trap
steps.instructions: Check the water trap for: Overfilling; Condensate; Blood or secretion contamination; Cracks or physical damage; Loose seating; Damaged seals; Incorrect or incompatible water-trap type. Empty or replace the water trap according to the applicable instructions. Ensure the replacement is fully seated. Do not apply silicone spray or unapproved substances to the water-trap holder or seals. Expected: The water trap is clean, undamaged, correctly seated, and below its maximum fill level. A full, contaminated, damaged, or improperly seated water trap can interfere with patient-gas measurement. If replacement corrects the FiO2 reading, complete the system test and stop.

steps.title: 7. Check the Breathing Circuit and Fresh-Gas Settings
steps.instructions: Verify that: Inspiratory and expiratory hoses are connected to the correct ports. The breathing circuit has no obvious disconnection or major leak. The CO2 absorber is properly installed. The fresh-gas O2 setting matches the intended bench-test condition. There is sufficient fresh-gas flow to change the circuit concentration. The circuit has been allowed enough time to reach the newly selected concentration. Expected: The breathing circuit is correctly assembled and produces a stable, plausible oxygen concentration. At low fresh-gas flows, the measured inspiratory oxygen concentration may not immediately equal the selected fresh-gas concentration. Allow the circuit concentration to stabilize before declaring the reading inaccurate. If correcting the circuit or allowing adequate stabilization resolves the discrepancy, document and stop.

steps.title: 8. Check for Contamination or Recent Reprocessing
steps.instructions: Ask whether the problem started after: Water-trap replacement; Breathing-system reassembly; Cleaning or disinfection; Aerosol or nebulizer use; Liquid entering the sample line; A major condensation event. Inspect only externally accessible components. Do not open the patient-gas measurement module. Expected: No evidence is found of liquid, aerosol, disinfectant, silicone, or other contamination entering the sampling path. Evidence of internal contamination requires repair evaluation.

steps.title: 9. Perform the Full System Test
steps.instructions: Place the machine in Standby with no patient connected. Prepare the machine according to the on-screen checklist and initiate the complete system test. Do not substitute only a breathing-system leakage test when the complaint involves O2 calibration. If the test stops: Record the displayed component and failure message. Correct any identified external condition. Repeat the affected test. Do not accept an O2-related irregularity merely to obtain a completed test result. Expected: The O2 measurement and associated gas-measurement functions display a successful result. If the complete test passes, continue with independent verification before returning the machine to service.

steps.title: 10. Verify the FiO2 Reading Independently
steps.instructions: Using the facility’s approved performance-verification procedure: Connect a test lung or approved test setup. Compare the Perseus FiO2 reading with a calibrated independent oxygen analyzer. Verify performance at ambient air and at a controlled high-O2 concentration. Allow both systems to stabilize before comparing values. Apply the acceptance limits in the current manufacturer service documentation. Expected: The displayed FiO2 agrees with the independent analyzer within the applicable tolerance. If the machine passes consistently, return it to service according to department policy.

steps.title: 11. Check for Intermittent Failure
steps.instructions: Repeat the system test or controlled gas verification sufficiently to determine whether the problem is intermittent. Review: Previous system-test results; Alarm history; Whether the reading drifts over time; Whether movement of the sample line affects the value; Whether the problem returns after warm-up; Whether multiple gases are reading incorrectly. Expected: The problem either remains corrected or can be reproduced reliably. Multiple inaccurate gas values may indicate a broader patient-gas measurement problem rather than an isolated O2 issue.

CCR.Complaint: Anesthesia reported that the Perseus displayed an unexpectedly low FiO2 and failed the O2 portion of the system test.
CCR.Cause: The water trap was overfilled and the sample line contained moisture, restricting gas sampling and producing an inaccurate oxygen measurement.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the machine from service, replaced the water trap and sample line, completed the full system test, verified FiO2 against a calibrated analyzer, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the problem occurred during startup or patient use
O2 pipeline and cylinder pressure status
Selected fresh-gas O2 concentration and flow

title: Drager Perseus Anesthesia Machine - CO2 or Anesthetic Agent Gas Measurement Unavailable
description: Troubleshooting unavailable CO2 or anesthetic-agent measurements caused by sample-line, filter, water-trap, startup-test, accessory, or internal gas-sensor faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended gas-measurement troubleshooting while the Perseus is supporting an active patient. If CO2 or anesthetic-agent monitoring becomes unavailable during a procedure: Alert the anesthesia provider immediately. Provide an approved independent gas-monitoring system or transfer the patient to another verified anesthesia machine. Maintain continuous oxygenation, ventilation, and appropriate anesthetic monitoring. Do not assume ventilation or agent delivery is safe solely because the machine continues operating. Drager specifies that O2, CO2, and anesthetic gases must be monitored whenever the breathing system is used. If the internal patient-gas measurement module fails, an independent gas-measurement system is required. Expected: Patient care is no longer dependent on the unavailable internal gas measurements. If alternate monitoring or equipment resolves the immediate safety concern, continue troubleshooting off patient.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Mode
steps.instructions: Review what clinical staff observed and record the complete alarm message. Determine whether: CO2 waveform and values are both absent. Anesthetic-agent values alone are unavailable. All patient-gas measurements are unavailable. Values appear briefly and then disappear. The failure began during startup, after circuit replacement, or during a case. The machine displays Sample line disconnected?, Sample line occluded, Water trap disconnected?, Water trap full, CO2 sensor accuracy low, or Gas sensor failure. The Perseus identifies disconnected or blocked sampling components separately from internal gas-sensor failures. Expected: The complaint is narrowed to a sampling-path problem, isolated measurement problem, or complete gas-analyzer failure. If the reported condition was resolved after correcting an obvious disconnected sampling line, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 3. Confirm Normal Power and Startup Status
steps.instructions: With the machine removed from active patient use: Confirm the Perseus is connected to reliable AC power. Check for unrelated startup, power, temperature, or cooling alarms. Place the unit in Standby according to facility procedure. Review the most recent system-test results for failed or incomplete gas-measurement items. If the machine recently froze or experienced an abnormal shutdown, perform a controlled restart and repeat the system test. Do not interrupt power while the machine is supporting a patient. Expected: The machine starts normally and either passes the gas-measurement portion of the system test or produces a repeatable failure. If gas measurement returns and the complete test passes, perform a controlled functional verification before returning the unit to service.

steps.title: 4. Check the Sample-Line Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect both ends of the sampling line. Verify that the line is: Securely connected at the Y-piece, HME filter, patient-side filter, or approved hose adapter. Securely connected to the water trap. Routed without tension or sharp bends. Installed without unauthorized adapters. The correct compatible sampling line for the Perseus. Drager directs that the sample line be securely connected at the patient-side sampling point and water trap, with no adapters used. An improperly connected or damaged line can cause faulty measurements. Expected: The sample line is firmly connected and correctly routed. If reseating the line restores stable CO2 and agent measurements, complete the system test and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Sample Line for Occlusion or Damage
steps.instructions: Examine the full length of the sampling line for: Kinks or compression. Internal condensation. Fluid contamination. Cracks or loose fittings. Discoloration or residue. Damage caused by equipment movement. Replace a questionable line with an approved new sample line rather than attempting to flush, clean, or disinfect it. Drager identifies sample lines as single-use items and warns that disinfectants can damage the sampling components. Expected: A clean, dry, unobstructed sampling path is established. If replacing the sample line restores the measurements, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 6. Check the Patient-Side Filter or Sampling Port
steps.instructions: Inspect the filter, HME, elbow, or adapter where the sample line connects. Look for: Condensation blocking the sampling port. Secretions or contamination. A protective cap left installed. A damaged or incompatible filter. A loose sampling connection. An incorrect sampling location. Replace a wet, blocked, contaminated, or questionable patient-side accessory with a compatible component. The manufacturer’s remedies for sample-line disconnection or occlusion specifically include checking the sample line, water trap, and patient-side filter. Expected: Gas can move freely from the patient connection through the sampling line. If the values return after replacing the filter or HME, complete verification and stop.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Water Trap
steps.instructions: Check whether the water trap is: Full or overfilled. Contaminated. Cracked or physically damaged. Expired. Incorrectly seated in its holder. The correct compatible type. Missing its required membrane or internal components. Empty or replace the water trap according to its instructions for use. Reseat it fully and confirm that any Water trap disconnected? or Water trap full alarm clears. A full, damaged, contaminated, or improperly connected water trap can interrupt or distort gas measurement. Do not apply silicone spray, aerosol cleaner, or lubricant to the water-trap holder or O-rings. Drager warns that silicone can disrupt measurement and silicone or aerosol residue may create a fire risk. Expected: The water trap is clean, correctly seated, within its replacement interval, and free of excess fluid. If replacement restores measurements, complete the system test and stop.

steps.title: 8. Distinguish Agent Measurement From Vaporizer Recognition
steps.instructions: If CO2 measurement works but anesthetic-agent information is unavailable, determine whether the complaint involves: Actual inspiratory or expiratory agent concentration. Vaporizer type recognition. Vaporizer dial-position display. Vaporizer filling-level display. Agent-prediction information. Inspect the vaporizer externally and confirm that it is: Correctly mounted and locked. Hanging vertically. Filled with the correct agent. Set to the intended concentration when testing is authorized. Free of obvious leakage or physical damage. The optional Vapor View system provides vaporizer identification, dial-position, filling-level, and prediction information. A Vapor View failure is therefore different from a failure of the patient-gas measurement module. Expected: The complaint is correctly classified as vaporizer recognition, agent delivery, or measured-agent concentration failure. If the problem is limited to a persistent Vapor View hardware alarm, document it separately and escalate according to the displayed alarm guidance.

steps.title: 9. Perform the System Test
steps.instructions: After correcting or replacing external sampling components: Configure the machine with an approved breathing circuit and test lung. Confirm the sample line and water trap are correctly installed. Keep the vaporizer off unless agent testing is specifically required and authorized. Run the complete Perseus system test. Review all gas-measurement results and alarms. Confirm that no gas-sensor, sampling-path, or water-trap alarm returns. Drager warns that a device with nonoperational CO2 or anesthetic-agent sensors requires suitable substitute monitoring before clinical use. Expected: The system test completes successfully without unresolved gas-measurement faults. If the system test repeatedly reports a sensor failure, stop troubleshooting and escalate.

steps.title: 10. Perform a Controlled Measurement Verification
