steps.title: 4. Inspect Gas Hoses and External Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect oxygen and air hoses, fittings, and accessible connection points for: Damage Loose fittings Kinks Contamination Incorrect connection Obvious leakage Expected outcome: External gas connections are correct, secure, and unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Verify Circuit and Test Setup
steps.instructions: Inspect the patient circuit and test configuration. Confirm accessories, humidification components, filters, and sampling or measurement devices are installed correctly and are not introducing a leak or misleading measurement. Expected outcome: The test setup is suitable for evaluating delivered oxygen concentration.

steps.title: 6. Perform the Approved Oxygen Calibration
steps.instructions: With the ventilator removed from patient use, perform the normal approved oxygen calibration applicable to the installed configuration. Do not repeatedly force calibration if the device consistently reports failure. Expected outcome: Calibration completes normally. If it passes and subsequent FiO2 verification is satisfactory, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Compare With an Independent Oxygen Analyzer
steps.instructions: When incorrect FiO2 is suspected, use an appropriate calibrated oxygen analyzer and approved test setup to compare delivered oxygen against the ventilator's displayed value. Avoid assuming the ventilator is incorrect until the independent measurement setup has also been verified. Expected outcome: Delivered and displayed oxygen values behave consistently with the selected test conditions. Significant unexplained disagreement requires further evaluation.

steps.title: 8. Check Accessible Sensor or Consumable Components
steps.instructions: If the installed configuration includes an externally serviceable oxygen-sensing component, inspect it for age-related deterioration, contamination, moisture, improper installation, or damage. Replace only with an approved compatible component and only when permitted by service procedure. Expected outcome: External oxygen-sensing components are correctly installed and serviceable.

steps.title: 9. Verify Configuration and Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm the selected oxygen setting, ventilation mode, and accessible configuration correspond to the intended test. Do not alter restricted calibration parameters or service-level configuration without authorized documentation. Expected outcome: No incorrect setting or configuration explains the reported discrepancy.

steps.title: 10. Complete Final Verification or Escalate
steps.instructions: After correction, verify oxygen calibration, delivered FiO2 using approved test equipment, normal ventilation, and associated alarms. If oxygen delivery remains unstable or cannot be verified, remove the ventilator from service. Expected outcome: Oxygen delivery is verified and stable, allowing troubleshooting to stop, or the ventilator is escalated appropriately.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the Babylog VN800 displayed an unexpected FiO2 and oxygen calibration would not complete.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the oxygen supply hose incompletely connected at the ventilator inlet.
CCR.Resolution: The oxygen hose was securely reconnected, calibration completed successfully, and delivered FiO2 was verified with an approved oxygen analyzer.

title: Drager Babylog VN800 Ventilator - System Check or Pre-Use Check Failure
description: Addresses failed pre-use or system checks caused by setup, circuit, accessory, gas supply, connection, or configuration problems before clinical use.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the Ventilator From Active Use
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a Babylog VN800 that is providing unreliable ventilation or alarming unexpectedly while a patient depends on it. Transfer ventilation to another verified device or approved alternate method before continuing. Inspect for obvious damage, contamination, liquid intrusion, overheating, unusual odor, or other unsafe conditions. Expected outcome: The patient is supported by reliable equipment and the Babylog VN800 is available for safe troubleshooting. If physical or electrical damage is present, remove the ventilator from service and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Check That Failed
steps.instructions: Repeat or review the reported system/pre-use check only when the ventilator is disconnected from a patient. Record the displayed failure description and identify which portion of the check does not complete. Determine whether the failure is repeatable or occurred only once. Expected outcome: A specific failed check or repeatable symptom is identified. If the check completes normally after correcting an obvious setup issue, complete final verification and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Power and Normal Startup
steps.instructions: Confirm the ventilator is connected to known-good facility power and that the power cord and external connections are secure and undamaged. Restart the ventilator normally if appropriate and observe whether startup completes without abnormal messages or interruptions. Expected outcome: The ventilator powers normally and reaches its expected operational state. If power remains unstable or startup is abnormal, remove the device from service for bench evaluation.

steps.title: 4. Verify Gas Supplies
steps.instructions: Confirm the required gas hoses are fully connected at the ventilator and wall or source connections. Inspect hoses and fittings for damage, loose connections, kinks, or obvious leakage. Verify the facility gas source is available using an appropriate known-good comparison or approved test method when needed. Expected outcome: Required gas sources are available and securely connected. If correcting a gas connection allows the system check to pass, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Patient Circuit and External Components
steps.instructions: Confirm the patient circuit is assembled correctly for the intended setup. Inspect tubing, connectors, adapters, humidification components, filters, test lungs, and other installed accessories for: Loose connections Incorrect assembly Cracks or damage Occlusions Missing components Water accumulation Incompatible or questionable accessories Expected outcome: The complete external breathing circuit is correctly assembled, unobstructed, and secure. If correcting the circuit resolves the check failure, proceed to final functional verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Flow Sensor and Expiratory Components
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible flow-sensing components and the expiratory valve assembly for correct installation, seating, cleanliness, dryness, and visible damage. Do not disassemble beyond normal operator-removable components or attempt internal sensor repair. Expected outcome: Flow-sensing and expiratory components are properly installed and recognized. If reseating or replacing an approved external component allows the check to pass, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Use Known-Good External Components When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the failed portion appears associated with an external circuit component, substitute a compatible known-good component one item at a time, such as an approved circuit, sensor, valve assembly, hose, or accessory. Repeat the applicable system check after each meaningful substitution. Expected outcome: A defective external component is isolated or ruled out. If the check passes with a known-good replacement, replace the failed external component and perform return-to-service testing.

steps.title: 8. Verify Configuration and Test Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm the ventilator is configured for the installed accessories and intended test setup. Check that required components are connected before initiating the system check. Do not enter restricted service menus or change configuration values without authorization and manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: The physical setup and accessible configuration agree. If correcting a configuration mismatch resolves the failure, repeat the complete required check.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting the identified issue, repeat the complete applicable system/pre-use check and verify normal ventilation using an appropriate test lung or approved analyzer as required by your facility procedure. Verify displayed measurements and alarm functions are reasonable for the test setup. Expected outcome: The Babylog VN800 completes required checks and demonstrates stable operation without recurring faults. Troubleshooting can stop and the device may proceed through normal return-to-service requirements.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Failure
steps.instructions: If the system/pre-use check continues to fail after external setup, supplies, circuit components, accessories, and configuration have been ruled out, do not repeatedly bypass or ignore the failure. Expected outcome: An unresolved ventilator is removed from service rather than returned to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the Babylog VN800 repeatedly failed its pre-use system check before patient setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a patient circuit connection incompletely seated, causing the circuit portion of the check to fail.
CCR.Resolution: The connection was secured, the system check was repeated successfully, and ventilator operation was verified with a test lung before return to service.

title: Drager Babylog VN800 Ventilator - Touchscreen, Display, or Control Input Unresponsive
description: Addresses frozen, blank, delayed, or unresponsive display and control input caused by power, startup, contamination, accessories, environment, or system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Transfer Ventilation if Control Is Unreliable
steps.instructions: If the touchscreen, display, or controls cannot be reliably used while the ventilator supports a patient, move the patient to another verified ventilator or approved alternate ventilation method. A ventilator with unreliable controls should not remain in patient service. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation is maintained with equipment that can be reliably monitored and controlled.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: Blank display Frozen display Touchscreen not responding Delayed response Incorrect touch location Specific control inputs not responding Intermittent loss of input Repeated startup freeze Record when the condition occurs. Expected outcome: The control or display problem is clearly characterized.

steps.title: 3. Verify Power and Startup
steps.instructions: Confirm the ventilator is connected to known-good AC power and observe the normal startup sequence. Check whether the display initializes, indicators illuminate, and the unit responds consistently. Expected outcome: The ventilator starts normally. Persistent startup or display failure requires removal from service.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Display and Touch Surface
steps.instructions: Inspect the touchscreen and surrounding bezel for: Fluid Cleaning residue Adhesive film Cracks Impact damage Foreign material Objects pressing against the screen Clean only according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: The screen is clean, dry, unobstructed, and physically intact.

steps.title: 5. Remove External Mechanical Interference
steps.instructions: Verify no accessory, cable, mounting bracket, cover, or nearby equipment is contacting the touchscreen or controls. Check that the display assembly is positioned normally and is not under mechanical stress. Expected outcome: No external object interferes with control input.

steps.title: 6. Perform a Normal Restart Off-Patient
steps.instructions: With the ventilator removed from patient use, perform a normal shutdown and restart if the system permits. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a ventilator that exhibits unusual heat, odor, electrical noise, or physical damage. Expected outcome: Controls and display resume normal operation. If the symptom does not recur, continue with extended functional verification before stopping.

steps.title: 7. Check for Intermittent Behavior
steps.instructions: Operate accessible touchscreen controls through normal menus and functions without altering unauthorized settings. Observe whether unresponsiveness is limited to one area, one control, or the entire interface. Expected outcome: The issue is either resolved, localized, or confirmed as a broader interface failure.

steps.title: 8. Verify Connected External Accessories
steps.instructions: If external communication or accessory connections were present when the problem occurred, disconnect nonessential accessories from the off-patient ventilator when permitted and retest. This helps distinguish a local control problem from an external accessory or communication interaction. Expected outcome: The display and controls remain stable with essential configuration only, or the problem persists independently.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: If responsiveness returns, operate the ventilator with a test lung and confirm controls respond consistently, the display updates correctly, alarms can be observed and acknowledged normally, and no freeze recurs. Expected outcome: The user interface remains stable during functional operation. Troubleshooting can stop after return-to-service requirements are met.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Any Persistent or Intermittent Control Failure
steps.instructions: A ventilator with recurring frozen screens, blank displays, unreliable touch input, or control response should not be returned to clinical use based solely on a temporary restart. Expected outcome: An unreliable ventilator is removed from service for bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the Babylog VN800 touchscreen stopped responding to input during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found cleaning residue and moisture remaining on the touchscreen surface and bezel.
CCR.Resolution: The screen was cleaned and dried using the approved method, control response remained stable through functional testing, and the ventilator passed final operational verification.

helpfulDetails: Blank, frozen, delayed, or unresponsive condition

title: Drager Babylog VN600 Ventilator - Air or O2 Gas Supply Failure
description: Addresses loss or instability of air or oxygen supply caused by wall outlets, hoses, fittings, connections, or upstream gas infrastructure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Ventilation
steps.instructions: A gas supply failure can immediately affect ventilation and oxygen delivery. Transfer the patient to another verified ventilator or appropriate backup source if the ventilator cannot reliably provide required support. Do not troubleshoot a questionable gas supply while a patient depends on the ventilator. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation and oxygenation are maintained safely. Once alternate support is established, troubleshooting may continue.

steps.title: 2. Identify Which Gas Supply Is Affected
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the reported problem involves: Air Oxygen Both gas supplies Intermittent gas loss A supply alarm with apparently normal wall gas Observe the ventilator's external connections and available indications without assuming the problem is internal. Expected outcome: The affected gas source and failure pattern are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Wall Outlet or External Gas Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the gas hose is connected to the intended wall outlet or approved external source. Check whether other equipment supplied from the same infrastructure is experiencing similar problems when appropriate. If permitted, test using another verified gas outlet. Expected outcome: A functional gas source is confirmed. If changing to a verified outlet resolves the problem, the ventilator may not be the cause and troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Gas Hoses
steps.instructions: Inspect air and oxygen hoses from end to end for: Kinks Crushing Cuts Loose fittings Damaged connectors Incorrect connections Excessive strain Reseat each connection securely. Expected outcome: Gas hoses are intact, unrestricted, and fully connected. If correcting a hose condition restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Substitute a Known-Good Hose
steps.instructions: If available, substitute a known-good approved gas hose for the affected supply. Change only one component at a time. Expected outcome: If normal gas supply is restored with the known-good hose, remove the defective hose from use and stop troubleshooting after ventilator verification.

steps.title: 6. Compare With Another Gas Outlet
steps.instructions: Where facility policy allows, connect the affected gas hose to another verified outlet of the correct gas type. This helps distinguish the ventilator and hose from an upstream infrastructure issue. Expected outcome: If the ventilator operates normally from another outlet, escalate the original outlet or pipeline issue to the appropriate facility department rather than repairing the ventilator.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Ventilator Gas Inlet Externally
steps.instructions: Inspect the accessible inlet and fitting for visible contamination, damage, looseness, or obstruction. Do not insert tools into gas pathways or disassemble internal pneumatic components. Expected outcome: The inlet appears intact and accepts the connector normally. Any visible inlet damage requires removal from service.

steps.title: 8. Verify Operation With Controlled Test Equipment
steps.instructions: After restoring the gas source, perform appropriate system checks and controlled ventilation testing. Verify oxygen delivery, pressure generation, alarms, and other required functions using approved equipment. Expected outcome: The ventilator operates normally with stable required gas supplies. If all verification passes, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Babylog VN600 repeatedly indicated loss of oxygen supply.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the oxygen hose connector was loose at the wall outlet.
CCR.Resolution: The oxygen hose was securely reconnected, gas supply indications normalized, and system and ventilation checks passed before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Other devices affected by the same outlet

title: Drager Babylog VN600 Ventilator - Apnea, Low Minute Volume, or Low Tidal Volume Alarm
description: Addresses low-volume or apnea alarms caused by disconnection, leakage, circuit problems, sensor issues, settings, patient interaction, or measurement errors.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Confirm Adequate Ventilation
steps.instructions: Apnea and low-volume alarms may indicate inadequate ventilation. Clinical staff should immediately assess the patient. If ventilation is inadequate or the ventilator's reliability is uncertain, move the patient to another verified ventilator or approved backup ventilation before technical troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Adequate patient ventilation is maintained independently. Technical troubleshooting can proceed safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Alarm
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint is: Apnea alarm Low minute volume Low tidal volume Intermittent low-volume readings Multiple related alarms Record whether the alarm occurred during spontaneous breathing, controlled ventilation, handling, suctioning, or circuit movement. Expected outcome: The specific alarm condition and circumstances are known.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Circuit Disconnection
steps.instructions: Trace the breathing circuit from the ventilator toward the patient connection. Check all joints, adapters, filters, humidification components, and sensor interfaces for loose or partially disconnected fittings. Expected outcome: The circuit is securely connected. If reconnecting a loose component restores normal volumes and stops the alarm, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect for External Leaks
steps.instructions: Check circuit tubing and accessories for: Cracks Split tubing Loose caps or ports Poorly seated connectors Damaged adapters Open sampling or accessory ports Use approved leak testing where appropriate. Expected outcome: No significant unintended external leak is present. If correcting the leak restores expected volume readings, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Flow Sensor
steps.instructions: Verify the flow sensor is properly seated, dry, clean, and undamaged. A contaminated, wet, or incorrectly installed sensor may affect tidal-volume and minute-volume measurement. Expected outcome: The sensor is correctly installed and measurement is stable. If sensor correction resolves the alarm, troubleshooting can stop after calibration and verification.

steps.title: 6. Check Circuit Positioning and Water Accumulation
steps.instructions: Inspect for tubing that is compressed, kinked, pulled loose, or holding significant condensate. Correct routing or replace affected components as appropriate. Expected outcome: The breathing circuit remains open and stable throughout normal positioning. If this resolves the alarm, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Review Alarm and Ventilation Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm alarm settings and ventilation configuration match the intended clinical setup. Do not independently alter prescribed therapeutic parameters. Have questionable patient-specific settings reviewed by the clinical team. Expected outcome: The alarm is not caused by an unintended setting or configuration mismatch.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Known-Good Circuit or Test Lung
steps.instructions: When appropriate, connect a known-good approved circuit and suitable test lung or ventilator analyzer. Observe delivered and measured tidal volume, minute volume, respiratory activity, and alarms. Expected outcome: The ventilator produces stable measurements and appropriate alarms under controlled conditions. If so, the original issue was likely external, circuit-related, or clinical.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Complete the applicable operational checks after correction. Verify delivered volumes, displayed measurements, flow sensing, circuit integrity, and alarm operation using approved test equipment. Expected outcome: Volume measurements and apnea detection behave normally and required return-to-service checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported repeated low tidal volume alarms on the Babylog VN600.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a partially disconnected circuit adapter creating an external leak.
CCR.Resolution: The adapter was securely reconnected, circuit integrity was verified, and delivered volume and alarm performance passed bench testing before return to service.

title: Drager Babylog VN600 Ventilator - Battery Not Charging or Short Runtime
description: Addresses charging failures or reduced battery runtime caused by AC power, connections, charging conditions, battery condition, or external power problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Reliable Power
steps.instructions: Do not allow a patient to depend on a ventilator with unreliable backup power during transport or any situation where AC power could be interrupted. If battery reliability is uncertain during active use, move the patient to another verified ventilator or maintain the device on a verified power source while clinical staff arrange safe continuity of care. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation is not dependent on the questionable battery. If reliable power cannot be assured, remove the ventilator from clinical use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Battery Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue is: Battery not charging Charge level not increasing Battery discharges rapidly Ventilator shuts down sooner than expected Battery is not recognized Problem occurs only during transport Record the displayed battery status and indications. Expected outcome: The exact battery-related symptom is identified and reproducible.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Connect the ventilator to a known-good AC outlet. Inspect the power cord for damage and confirm it is fully seated at both ends. If appropriate, test the outlet using approved electrical test equipment. Expected outcome: Reliable AC power reaches the ventilator. If charging begins normally after correcting the outlet or power connection, troubleshooting can stop after battery verification.

steps.title: 4. Observe Charging Indications
steps.instructions: With the ventilator connected to verified AC power, observe whether the device indicates external power and battery charging. Allow sufficient normal charging opportunity before evaluating runtime. Expected outcome: The ventilator recognizes AC operation and shows expected charging behavior. If charging proceeds normally, continue to verify battery performance.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Battery Components
steps.instructions: Where the battery is user-accessible and removal is permitted, inspect it and its external contacts for: Damage Swelling Cracks Contamination Corrosion Improper seating Do not use a visibly damaged or swollen battery. Expected outcome: The battery is intact and correctly installed. A damaged battery is removed from service immediately.

steps.title: 6. Reseat or Substitute the Battery Where Applicable
steps.instructions: If permitted by the device configuration and facility procedure, reseat the battery. When available, substitute a known-good approved battery. Expected outcome: If charging and runtime normalize with the known-good battery, the original battery is the likely cause and should be replaced according to facility policy.

steps.title: 7. Evaluate Battery Runtime Using an Approved Procedure
steps.instructions: After the battery has been appropriately charged, perform battery testing using the applicable manufacturer or facility-approved method. Do not estimate battery condition solely from the displayed percentage. Expected outcome: Battery performance meets the required return-to-service criteria. If it does, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Check for Intermittent External Power Loss
steps.instructions: Gently inspect the external power connection for looseness without stressing the cable or connector. Confirm that normal equipment movement does not cause unintended switching between AC and battery operation. Expected outcome: External power remains stable during normal positioning. If a damaged cord or loose external connection is identified and corrected, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction, verify AC operation, battery charging, transfer between AC and battery as permitted, battery indications, alarms, and required operational checks. Expected outcome: The ventilator operates reliably on its intended power sources and battery performance meets applicable requirements.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Babylog VN600 battery discharged quickly during transport preparation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the installed battery failed the approved battery performance test while a known-good battery performed normally.
CCR.Resolution: The degraded battery was replaced, charging and battery operation were verified, and the ventilator passed final functional testing before return to service.

title: Drager Babylog VN600 Ventilator - Expiratory Valve Not Recognized or Not Seated
description: Addresses expiratory valve recognition or seating problems caused by installation, contamination, moisture, component damage, incompatibility, or external interface issues.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the Ventilator From Active Use
steps.instructions: An expiratory valve problem may affect pressure control, exhalation, and ventilation. Do not troubleshoot the valve while a patient depends on the ventilator. Transfer the patient to another verified ventilator or appropriate backup method. Expected outcome: The patient is safely ventilated using alternate equipment and the Babylog VN600 can be inspected off-patient.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Verify whether the ventilator reports that the expiratory valve is absent, incorrectly installed, or otherwise unavailable. Record any displayed message and determine whether the problem occurs consistently. Expected outcome: The valve recognition problem is confirmed. If reseating during normal setup immediately resolves the message and system checks pass, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Remove and Inspect the Expiratory Valve
steps.instructions: Following approved handling procedures, remove the externally accessible valve assembly and inspect for: Incorrect assembly Visible contamination Moisture Cracks Warping Damaged mating surfaces Foreign material Do not disassemble the valve beyond manufacturer-approved user-accessible components. Expected outcome: The valve is clean, dry, intact, and correctly assembled. Any visibly damaged component should be removed from use.

steps.title: 4. Verify Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm the installed expiratory component is approved and appropriate for the Babylog VN600 configuration. Do not force an incompatible or poorly fitting component into the ventilator. Expected outcome: The correct compatible expiratory component is being used. If replacing an incorrect component resolves the issue, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Reinstall the Valve Carefully
steps.instructions: Reinstall the valve according to the normal manufacturer-approved installation process. Confirm it sits fully in position without resistance or unusual looseness. Expected outcome: The valve seats normally and is recognized by the ventilator. If recognition returns and the system check passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Valve Interface
steps.instructions: Inspect the accessible valve mounting area and contact surfaces for moisture, contamination, foreign material, or visible damage. Do not insert tools into internal pneumatic pathways. Expected outcome: The accessible interface is clean, dry, and undamaged. If correcting contamination restores recognition, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Expiratory Valve
steps.instructions: Install a known-good approved valve assembly when available. Repeat the relevant system check. Expected outcome: If the known-good valve is recognized normally, the original valve assembly is the likely cause. Remove it from use and stop troubleshooting after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Inspect Related Circuit Connections
steps.instructions: Verify the breathing circuit is correctly connected around the expiratory pathway and that no accessory is pulling, twisting, or displacing the valve assembly. Expected outcome: The valve remains correctly seated during normal circuit positioning. If routing correction resolves the issue, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Complete the required system/pre-use check after correction. Using approved test equipment, verify ventilation, pressure control, expiratory function, leakage, and alarm operation as applicable. Expected outcome: The valve remains recognized and the ventilator passes required checks. The device may be returned to service after successful verification.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Babylog VN600 would not recognize the installed expiratory valve.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the expiratory valve was not fully seated in its mounting position.
CCR.Resolution: The valve was removed, inspected, correctly reinstalled, and the ventilator passed its system check and functional ventilation testing before return to service.

title: Drager Babylog VN600 Ventilator - Flow Sensor Calibration Failure
description: Addresses flow sensor calibration failures caused by sensor condition, installation, circuit setup, contamination, moisture, connections, or incompatible external components.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Ventilation
steps.instructions: If unreliable flow measurement affects active patient ventilation, monitoring, or alarms, move the patient to another verified ventilator or appropriate backup ventilation before troubleshooting. Do not attempt calibration while a patient depends on the affected measurement system. Expected outcome: The patient is safely supported and the ventilator is available for controlled testing. If safe patient support cannot be maintained, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Calibration Failure
steps.instructions: Identify whether the reported problem is a failed calibration, unstable flow reading, inaccurate displayed volume, or sensor recognition problem. Repeat the calibration only under the proper non-patient test conditions described by manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: The failure is reproducible and clearly associated with the flow measurement system. If calibration completes normally and subsequent measurements are verified, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Flow Sensor
steps.instructions: Remove and visually inspect the externally accessible flow sensor according to approved handling procedures. Check for: Moisture Condensation Secretions or contamination Cracks Bent or damaged contacts Improper assembly Incorrect sensor type Do not mechanically clean delicate sensing elements unless specifically permitted by manufacturer instructions. Expected outcome: The sensor is clean, dry, compatible, and undamaged. If correcting the sensor condition resolves calibration, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify Sensor Installation and Orientation
steps.instructions: Reinstall the flow sensor carefully and verify that it is fully seated and correctly oriented. Inspect associated external connectors or cables for loose connections, contamination, or visible damage. Expected outcome: The sensor is installed securely and recognized normally. If calibration succeeds after reseating, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Breathing Circuit
steps.instructions: Verify the breathing circuit is properly assembled and free of major leaks, occlusions, water accumulation, or incorrect adapters that could interfere with calibration. Confirm any required circuit components are installed in their intended positions. Expected outcome: The circuit is correctly configured and does not create an external condition that prevents flow calibration. If correction restores calibration, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Allow Wet Components to Dry or Replace Them
steps.instructions: If condensation or moisture is present, replace the affected flow sensor or circuit component with an approved dry component when appropriate. Do not use improvised drying methods that could damage the sensor. Expected outcome: Calibration is attempted with a clean, dry sensor and appropriate circuit. If calibration passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Flow Sensor
steps.instructions: Install a compatible known-good sensor if available. Repeat the calibration using the approved procedure. Expected outcome: If the known-good sensor calibrates normally, the original sensor or its condition is implicated. Replace or process the original component according to facility and manufacturer requirements, then stop troubleshooting after successful verification.

steps.title: 8. Check for External Connection Problems
steps.instructions: Inspect all accessible sensor interfaces for looseness, bent contacts, contamination, or cable strain. Do not open the ventilator or troubleshoot internal electronics. Expected outcome: External sensor interfaces are intact and stable. If correcting an external connection restores calibration, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After calibration succeeds, verify flow and volume measurements using appropriate approved test equipment and the applicable manufacturer procedure. Confirm alarms and ventilation performance operate normally. Expected outcome: Calibration completes successfully and measured performance is acceptable under the required return-to-service test. The ventilator may be returned to service when all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Babylog VN600 would not complete flow sensor calibration.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found condensation present in the installed flow sensor.
CCR.Resolution: The wet sensor was replaced with a clean approved sensor, calibration completed successfully, and flow and ventilation performance were verified before return to service.

title: Drager Babylog VN600 Ventilator - High Airway Pressure Alarm
description: Addresses high airway pressure alarms caused by circuit obstruction, secretions, water, tubing problems, accessories, settings, or patient-related resistance.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Assess the Clinical Situation
steps.instructions: A high airway pressure alarm can indicate an immediately unsafe patient or circuit condition. Clinical staff must assess the patient and maintain adequate ventilation. If the cause cannot be immediately identified or the ventilator appears unreliable, transfer the patient to another verified ventilator or approved backup ventilation before technical troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The patient is receiving adequate ventilation independently of the suspect ventilator. Clinical Engineering may then troubleshoot the equipment safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Whether the Alarm Is Patient-Related or Device-Related
steps.instructions: Obtain the circumstances of the alarm from clinical staff: Continuous or intermittent During inspiration or specific procedures After circuit repositioning After adding accessories Only with the patient connected Do not change prescribed ventilator settings as a troubleshooting shortcut. Expected outcome: The conditions that trigger the alarm are understood. If the alarm occurs only because of a verified clinical condition, management belongs with the clinical team.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Patient Circuit for Obstruction
steps.instructions: Check the entire external circuit for: Kinked tubing Crushed tubing Occluded filters Closed or blocked connectors Pinched tubing Incorrectly assembled components Correct any obvious obstruction. Expected outcome: The circuit is open and unobstructed. If removing the obstruction eliminates the alarm and performance verifies normally, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Check for Water Accumulation
steps.instructions: Inspect the circuit, water traps, humidification components, and dependent tubing for accumulated condensate that could restrict gas flow. Have contaminated or wet patient-use components handled according to infection-control procedures. Expected outcome: Excess water is removed or affected components are replaced according to approved practice. If pressures normalize, troubleshooting can stop after testing.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Filters and Accessories
steps.instructions: Verify filters, humidification components, adapters, valves, and other accessories are appropriate, correctly oriented, and not occluded. If appropriate, substitute a known-good approved component. Expected outcome: External accessories do not create excessive resistance. If known-good substitution resolves the alarm, remove the defective component from use and stop troubleshooting after verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Circuit Connections and Positioning
steps.instructions: Confirm tubing is routed without tension, bending, compression, or obstruction from bed rails, equipment, transport hardware, or nearby objects. Expected outcome: The circuit remains open throughout its full routing. If repositioning resolves the pressure alarm, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Verify Alarm and Ventilation Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm the high-pressure alarm limit and relevant ventilation settings match the intended clinical configuration. Clinical Engineering should not independently change prescribed therapeutic settings. Any questionable clinical settings should be reviewed with the respiratory or medical team. Expected outcome: The alarm is not being caused by an unintended configuration or inappropriate alarm setting.

steps.title: 8. Test the Ventilator Off-Patient
steps.instructions: Connect an appropriate test lung or ventilator analyzer and reproduce representative operating conditions. Observe airway pressure, flow, alarm activation, and pressure stability. Expected outcome: The ventilator operates without inappropriate high-pressure alarms under controlled testing. If it does, the original cause was likely external or patient-related.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction, complete required operational and alarm testing using approved equipment and manufacturer guidance. Verify pressure measurement, ventilation delivery, alarms, and circuit integrity. Expected outcome: Airway pressure behaves normally and alarms activate appropriately. The ventilator may be returned to service when all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported repeated high airway pressure alarms during use of the Babylog VN600.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the expiratory-side circuit tubing partially kinked beneath attached equipment.
CCR.Resolution: The tubing was rerouted to eliminate the restriction, and controlled ventilation and alarm testing confirmed normal pressure operation before return to service.

title: Drager Babylog VN600 Ventilator - Network or Data Communication Failure
description: Addresses loss of network or data communication caused by cables, ports, infrastructure, configuration, intermediary systems, or external connectivity problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Confirm Clinical Impact
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the communication failure affects only data transfer or also compromises required monitoring, alarms, or clinical workflow. Do not troubleshoot unreliable communication while clinicians are depending on the affected data path. Provide an alternate verified monitoring or documentation method when necessary. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely without depending on the failed communication pathway.

steps.title: 2. Define the Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine what is not communicating: Ventilator to network Ventilator to central monitoring Ventilator to device integration system Data not reaching the electronic record Intermittent connection No network indication Identify the last known point where data is successfully received. Expected outcome: The failed portion of the communication path is narrowed to a specific link or endpoint.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Ventilator Is Otherwise Operating Normally
steps.instructions: Confirm ventilation, alarms, display, and local measurements function correctly. A communication failure should not be treated as a network-only problem if other device functions are abnormal. Expected outcome: The Babylog VN600 operates normally except for data communication. If other functions are affected, remove the device from service and troubleshoot the broader failure.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the External Communication Cable
steps.instructions: Inspect the network or data cable for: Loose connectors Broken locking tabs Cuts Pinching Excessive strain Visible connector damage Reseat both ends when appropriate. Expected outcome: The cable is intact and securely connected. If communication returns after reseating, verify stable data transfer and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Substitute a Known-Good Cable
steps.instructions: If the connection uses a replaceable external cable, substitute a verified compatible cable. Expected outcome: If communication returns with the known-good cable, remove the defective cable from use and stop troubleshooting after end-to-end verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify the Network Port or External Endpoint
steps.instructions: Where permitted, test the connection using another known-good approved port or verify that the original network jack or intermediary connection is operational. Coordinate with Information Services or the appropriate integration team when infrastructure access is outside Clinical Engineering authority. Expected outcome: The external network endpoint is verified. If another port works normally, escalate the original infrastructure issue rather than assuming a ventilator failure.

steps.title: 7. Check Intermediate Communication Equipment
steps.instructions: If the data path includes an interface device, device adapter, network converter, docking connection, gateway, or integration appliance, verify: Power Cable seating Status indicators Physical connection Whether other devices using the same infrastructure are affected Do not alter protected configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The communication path is intact through each external component. A failed intermediary component is isolated if applicable.

steps.title: 8. Verify Authorized Network Configuration
steps.instructions: Compare the ventilator's authorized network or communication configuration with documented site requirements. Do not guess addresses, alter production network settings, or enter restricted service menus. Coordinate configuration changes with qualified Clinical Engineering, IT, integration, or manufacturer personnel as required. Expected outcome: The ventilator's documented configuration matches the intended communication environment.

steps.title: 9. Verify End-to-End Data Flow
steps.instructions: After correcting the connection, confirm that current ventilator data reaches the intended receiving system. Verify the correct device and patient context where applicable and ensure stale or previously cached data is not mistaken for live communication. Expected outcome: Current data is received correctly at the intended endpoint. If the full communication path is restored and stable, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm local ventilator operation remains normal after communication is restored. Verify ventilation, alarms, controls, network status, and the complete external data path as required by facility procedure. Expected outcome: The ventilator operates normally and current data reaches the intended destination consistently. The device may be returned to service when all required verification passes.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Babylog VN600 was operating normally but ventilator data was no longer reaching the connected monitoring system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a damaged external network cable between the ventilator connection and the facility network port.
CCR.Resolution: The damaged cable was replaced, live ventilator data was confirmed at the receiving system, and local ventilator operation was verified before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Last successful point in data path
Live data verified at receiving system

title: Drager Babylog VN600 Ventilator - O2 Sensor Calibration Failure or Incorrect FiO2
description: Addresses oxygen calibration failures or incorrect FiO2 caused by gas supply, connections, calibration conditions, external setup, or measurement problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Oxygen Delivery
steps.instructions: If delivered or displayed oxygen concentration is questionable while a patient is connected, immediately provide ventilation and oxygen using another verified device or approved backup method. Do not continue troubleshooting while a patient depends on an unreliable oxygen measurement or delivery system. Expected outcome: Patient oxygen delivery is maintained independently. If safe oxygen delivery cannot be assured, remove the ventilator from clinical use immediately.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint is: Oxygen calibration will not complete Displayed FiO2 is higher or lower than expected FiO2 fluctuates The ventilator reports an oxygen measurement problem Repeat the condition only under controlled bench conditions. Expected outcome: The exact oxygen-related symptom is identified and reproducible. If the problem cannot be reproduced and verification testing passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Oxygen and Air Supplies
steps.instructions: Confirm oxygen and air sources are available and connected to the correct gas inlets. Inspect external hoses, fittings, and wall connections for: Loose connections Damage Kinks Incorrect gas connection Signs of contamination If practical, compare operation using another verified outlet or known-good approved hose. Expected outcome: Correct gas sources are securely connected and available. If correcting a supply problem restores proper FiO2 and calibration, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Confirm Calibration Conditions
steps.instructions: Perform oxygen calibration only under the operating conditions required by the applicable manufacturer procedure. Avoid attempting to compensate for an incorrect gas supply by repeatedly recalibrating the ventilator. Expected outcome: Calibration is attempted under appropriate stable conditions. If calibration succeeds and oxygen output verifies normally, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Patient Circuit and External Components
steps.instructions: Verify the circuit, filters, humidification accessories, adapters, and gas-related external components are installed correctly and are not leaking or obstructed. Check for connections that could allow room air entrainment or otherwise affect measured oxygen concentration. Expected outcome: The breathing system is correctly assembled without an external leak or configuration problem affecting FiO2. If correction restores proper readings, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Compare Displayed FiO2 With Approved Test Equipment
steps.instructions: Using appropriate calibrated oxygen-analysis equipment, compare delivered oxygen concentration with the ventilator's displayed value during controlled bench operation. Do not use an unverified analyzer to condemn the ventilator. Expected outcome: Delivered and displayed oxygen behavior is consistent with the applicable verification procedure. If measurements are acceptable, the original complaint may have been setup-related and troubleshooting can stop after documentation.

steps.title: 7. Check for Pattern Changes Across FiO2 Settings
steps.instructions: Using approved test methods, verify whether the discrepancy occurs consistently or only under specific operating conditions. Do not make unauthorized calibration adjustments or enter restricted service modes. Expected outcome: Testing determines whether the problem is external and configuration-related or remains present across controlled conditions.

steps.title: 8. Verify External Sensor-Related Connections Where Accessible
steps.instructions: Inspect externally accessible oxygen measurement connections or related components for damage, looseness, or contamination where applicable. Do not open the ventilator or replace internal oxygen measurement components without authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: Accessible connections are secure and undamaged. If correcting an external connection resolves calibration or accuracy, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction, complete the appropriate system checks and verify oxygen delivery across representative operating conditions using approved test equipment. Confirm alarms and ventilation functions operate normally. Expected outcome: Oxygen calibration completes and delivered oxygen concentration verifies appropriately. The ventilator may be returned to service only after all required testing passes.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Babylog VN600 displayed an FiO2 value inconsistent with the expected oxygen setting.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the oxygen supply hose was not fully seated at the ventilator connection.
CCR.Resolution: The oxygen connection was secured, oxygen calibration completed successfully, and delivered FiO2 was verified with approved test equipment before return to service.

title: Drager Babylog VN600 Ventilator - System Check or Pre-Use Check Failure
description: Addresses failed system or pre-use checks caused by setup, circuit, accessory, gas supply, connection, or configuration problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Ventilation
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a Babylog VN600 that is providing unreliable ventilation or alarms while a patient depends on it. Transfer ventilation to another verified ventilator or appropriate backup method before continuing. Inspect the ventilator for obvious damage, contamination, fluid intrusion, unusual odor, excessive heat, or other unsafe conditions. Expected outcome: The patient is supported independently and the ventilator can be evaluated safely. If damage or another unsafe condition is present, remove the ventilator from service and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Check Failure
steps.instructions: Repeat or review the system/pre-use check only when the ventilator is disconnected from a patient. Record which portion of the check fails and any displayed message. Verify whether the failure is repeatable or occurred only once during setup. Expected outcome: The failed portion of the check is clearly identified. If the check passes normally on repeat and subsequent operation is verified, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power and Basic Startup
steps.instructions: Confirm the ventilator is connected to a known-good AC outlet and that the power cord and external connections are fully seated and undamaged. Observe startup for abnormal resets, blank displays, or incomplete initialization. Expected outcome: The ventilator powers and initializes normally without power-related interruptions. If correcting the power source resolves the system check failure, troubleshooting can stop after successful verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Gas Supplies
steps.instructions: Confirm required air and oxygen supplies are available and connected correctly. Inspect hoses and connectors for damage, loose fittings, kinks, or incorrect connections. If appropriate, compare operation using another verified gas outlet or known-good approved gas hose. Expected outcome: Required gas sources are present, stable, and correctly connected. If restoring the gas supply allows the check to pass, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Patient Circuit and Accessories
steps.instructions: Verify the breathing circuit is assembled correctly for the intended configuration. Inspect tubing, connectors, filters, humidification components, test lungs, adapters, and other external accessories for: Loose connections Cracks or splits Occlusions Incorrect assembly Water accumulation Missing components Reseat all accessible connections. Expected outcome: The circuit is complete, unobstructed, leak-free, and correctly assembled. If correcting the circuit allows the system check to pass, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Expiratory Valve and Flow Measurement Components
steps.instructions: Verify the expiratory valve and externally accessible flow-sensing components are the correct compatible items, properly installed, clean, dry, and fully seated. Do not force components into place or perform internal disassembly. Expected outcome: External measurement and expiratory components are recognized and correctly positioned. If reseating or replacing an approved external component resolves the check failure, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Known-Good External Components
steps.instructions: When available, substitute known-good approved breathing circuit components, filters, sensors, hoses, or expiratory components one at a time. Avoid changing several components simultaneously because this can obscure the cause. Expected outcome: A defective or incorrectly assembled external component is isolated. If the check passes with the known-good component and repeat testing is successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Verify Intended Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm the ventilator is configured for the installed circuit, accessories, and intended patient application without entering unauthorized service menus or altering protected settings. Correct only settings within normal Clinical Engineering authority and manufacturer-supported procedures. Expected outcome: Installed hardware and selected configuration are compatible. If correcting an external configuration mismatch resolves the failure, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Repeat the complete required system or pre-use check using the appropriate manufacturer documentation. Confirm normal startup, ventilation using suitable test equipment, alarm operation, displayed measurements, gas delivery, and accessory recognition as applicable. Expected outcome: The ventilator completes the required checks successfully and operates normally. Document the results and return the device to service only when all required verification passes.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Babylog VN600 repeatedly failed the pre-use system check before patient use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose patient-circuit connection that caused the system check to fail.
CCR.Resolution: The connection was properly seated, the complete system check was repeated successfully, and ventilator operation and alarms were verified before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact failed system-check step or displayed message

title: Drager Babylog VN600 Ventilator - Touchscreen, Display, or Control Input Unresponsive
description: Addresses frozen, blank, delayed, or unresponsive display and control input caused by power, connections, contamination, software state, or external damage.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Ventilation
steps.instructions: If the display or controls become unresponsive while a patient is connected, do not continue relying on a ventilator whose settings, alarms, or status cannot be reliably viewed or controlled. Move the patient to another verified ventilator or appropriate backup method before technical troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The patient is supported by reliable equipment and the affected ventilator is available for evaluation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Control Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue is: Blank display Frozen display Touch input not responding Delayed response Only part of the screen unresponsive Physical control not responding Intermittent behavior Record whether alarms remained active and whether ventilation continued. Expected outcome: The failure mode is clearly identified. If the control responds normally after a single transient event and all verification passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Display and Control Surface
steps.instructions: Check for: Fluid or cleaning residue Protective coverings interfering with touch Cracks Impact damage Foreign material Excessive pressure from attached accessories Clean only using approved methods. Expected outcome: The control surface is clean, dry, unobstructed, and undamaged. If removing contamination restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify AC Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the ventilator is connected to a known-good AC source and that the power cord is securely seated. Observe for intermittent power indications, resets, or unexpected switching to battery. Expected outcome: The ventilator receives stable power. If correcting an external power problem restores normal controls, troubleshooting can stop after functional testing.

steps.title: 5. Perform an Approved Restart Off-Patient
steps.instructions: With the ventilator removed from patient use, perform a normal shutdown and restart using the standard manufacturer-supported procedure. Do not force shutdowns or access unauthorized service functions. Expected outcome: The ventilator completes startup and the display and controls respond normally. If the condition does not recur and all required tests pass, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Check External Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect externally accessible display or system connections only where normal Clinical Engineering access is intended. Check for loose cables, damaged connectors, or accessories that may be interfering with operation. Do not open the display assembly or internal electronics. Expected outcome: External connections are secure and undamaged. If reseating an approved external connection resolves the problem, troubleshooting can stop after testing.

steps.title: 7. Remove Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential approved external peripherals or communication accessories one at a time where safe and supported. Restart or retest the ventilator as appropriate. Expected outcome: If the control system operates normally with a particular external accessory removed, isolate that accessory for further evaluation.

steps.title: 8. Verify Controls Under Bench Operation
steps.instructions: Operate the ventilator off-patient using a suitable test lung or analyzer. Check normal navigation, setting selection, alarm acknowledgement, display updates, and control response without changing protected service configuration. Expected outcome: Controls respond consistently without freezing, delay, or unintended activation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Complete required system checks and confirm the ventilator display, touchscreen, physical controls, alarms, ventilation, and status indicators operate normally. Expected outcome: All operator controls and displayed information remain stable and responsive throughout testing. The device may be returned to service when required tests pass.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Babylog VN600 touchscreen stopped responding during equipment setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried cleaning residue across the touchscreen surface that interfered with touch input.
CCR.Resolution: The display was cleaned using the approved method, normal touchscreen response returned, and system, control, alarm, and ventilation checks passed before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Blank, frozen, or partially responsive condition
